---

**TL;DR:** T-GM node cnfdf32 stuck in FREERUN (ClockClass 248) caused 27/28 failures; 1 independent FIFO test regression.

**Overall Issue Class:** infra_other
**Overall Severity:** HIGH

## Root Causes (28 failures across 6 suites)

### 23/28 failures — T-GM FREERUN cascade (log-stream timeouts)
- **Suites:** tgm, tbc, bc, dualfollower, dualnicbc, dualnicbcha | **Evidence:** PROVEN (tgm, tbc); HYPOTHESIS (bc, dualfollower, dualnicbc, dualnicbcha — unverified cascade)
- **What:** cnfdf32 reported ClockClass 248 on ens7fx instead of ClockClass 7 (GNSS-LOCKED) for the entire ~4-hour run. Downstream daemons never entered sync, so `linuxptp-daemon-container` never emitted LOCKED profile lines; the test log-stream poller hit `timedout waiting for matches` / `context deadline exceeded` on every node across all suites.
- **Breaking change:** Unknown — lab GNSS/ts2phc fault on cnfdf32. Candidate (unverified): linuxptp-daemon release-4.20 PR #629 (upstream sync 2026-07-22, commit `14eb788`) may have regressed ts2phc GNSS handling or log format.
- **Flake?** No — ClockClass 248 persisted across all 6 parallel suites from first to last test.
- **Fix:** Restore GNSS lock on cnfdf32, confirm ClockClass 7, then re-run.

### 4/28 failures — OS Clock never LOCKED (parallel sync tests)
- **Suites:** bc, dualfollower, dualnicbc, dualnicbcha | **Evidence:** PROVEN (direct consequence of Group 1)
- **What:** `Event based tests PTP Slave Clock Sync` in each suite's parallel phase timed out with `OS Clock was never LOCKED` — downstream effect of T-GM FREERUN; no independent root cause.
- **Breaking change:** Unknown (same infra cause as Group 1)
- **Flake?** No
- **Fix:** Same as Group 1; no independent action needed.

### 1/28 failures — FIFO scheduling assertion mismatch
- **Suites:** tbc | **Evidence:** PROVEN
- **What:** `Should check whether using fifo scheduling` asserts `HaveLen(0)` but finds `{"test-wpc-tbc_tbc-tr": 10, "test-wpc-tbc_tbc-tt": 10}`. TBC testdata profiles (`profile-tbc-tr.yaml:156-157`) explicitly set `ptpSchedulingPolicy: SCHED_FIFO` / priority 10, so the assertion is stale or the profiles changed unexpectedly. `check_backport.py` exited with error (exit 2); cannot attribute to a specific commit.
- **Breaking change:** Unknown — test assertion likely written against a prior profile state.
- **Flake?** No — deterministic mismatch.
- **Fix:** Confirm whether FIFO scheduling is intentional in TBC profiles; update `HaveLen(0)` or remove FIFO from profiles.

  restartPolicy: Never
  serviceAccountName: builder
  containers:
    - name: priv
      image: quay.io/podman/stable:v4.9.4
      command:
        - /bin/bash
        - -c
        - |
          set -xe
          yum install jq git wget podman-docker -y
          yum group install "development-tools" -y
          wget https://go.dev/dl/go1.20.4.linux-amd64.tar.gz
          rm -rf /usr/local/go && tar -C /usr/local -xzf go1.20.4.linux-amd64.tar.gz
          export PATH=$PATH:/usr/local/go/bin
          go version

          # set +x here to hide pass from log
          set +xe

          echo "podman login with serviceaccount"

          # Used for 4.16 and newer releases.
          pass=$( jq .\"image-registry.openshift-image-registry.svc:5000\".auth /var/run/secrets/openshift.io/push/.dockercfg )
          pass=`echo ${pass:1:-1} | base64 -d`
          podman login -u serviceaccount -p ${pass:8} image-registry.openshift-image-registry.svc:5000 --tls-verify=false

          # Used for 4.15 and older releases.
          if ! podman login --get-login image-registry.openshift-image-registry.svc:5000 &> /dev/null; then
            pass=$( jq .\"image-registry.openshift-image-registry.svc:5000\".password /var/run/secrets/openshift.io/push/.dockercfg )
            podman login -u serviceaccount -p ${pass:1:-1} image-registry.openshift-image-registry.svc:5000 --tls-verify=false
          fi

          set -x

          export IMG=PTP_IMAGE
          export DAEMON_IMG="DAEMON_IMAGE"
          export SIDECAR_IMG="SIDECAR_IMAGE"

          export T5CI_VERSION="T5CI_VERSION_VAL"
          export USE_UPSTREAM="USE_UPSTREAM_VAL"

          # run latest release on upstream main branch
          if [[ "${USE_UPSTREAM:-false}" == "true" ]]; then
            echo "Running on upstream main branch"
            git clone --single-branch --branch main https://github.com/k8snetworkplumbingwg/ptp-operator.git
          else
            git clone --single-branch --branch OPERATOR_VERSION https://github.com/openshift/ptp-operator.git
          fi
          cd ptp-operator
          # OCPBUGS-52327 fix build due to libresolv.so link error
          sed -i "s/\(CGO_ENABLED=\${CGO_ENABLED}\) \(GOOS=\${GOOS}\)/\1 CC=\"gcc -fuse-ld=gold\" \2/" hack/build.sh
          # For UPSTREAM use Dockerfile for upstream contents
          if [[ "$T5CI_VERSION" =~ 4.1[2-8]+ || "${USE_UPSTREAM:-false}" == "true" ]]; then
            sed -i "/ENV GO111MODULE=off/ a\ENV GOMAXPROCS=20" Dockerfile
            make docker-build
          else
            # Dockerfile is updated to upstream in 4.19+. Use .ocp or .ci versions for non-UPSTREAM runs
            if [ -f "Dockerfile.ocp" ]; then
              DOCKERFILE="Dockerfile.ocp"
            else
              DOCKERFILE="Dockerfile.ci"
            fi
            sed -i "/ENV GO111MODULE=off/ a\ENV GOMAXPROCS=20" "$DOCKERFILE"
            podman build -t "${IMG}" -f "$DOCKERFILE"
          fi
          podman push ${IMG} --tls-verify=false
          cd ..

          if [[ "${USE_UPSTREAM:-false}" == "false" ]]; then
            # If we a running a downstream run we are done
            exit 0
          fi

          # If were running upstream we should also use the upstream daemon!
          echo "Running on upstream main branch of linuxptp-daemon"
          git clone --single-branch --branch main https://github.com/k8snetworkplumbingwg/linuxptp-daemon.git
          cd linuxptp-daemon
          # Split DAEMON_IMG into IMAGE_TAG_BASE and VERSION because
          # hack/build-image.sh unconditionally overwrites IMG from these two vars.
          IMAGE_TAG_BASE="${DAEMON_IMG%:*}" VERSION="${DAEMON_IMG##*:}" make image
          podman push ${DAEMON_IMG} --tls-verify=false
          cd ..

          echo "Running on main branch of cloud-event-proxy"
          git clone --single-branch --branch main https://github.com/redhat-cne/cloud-event-proxy.git
          cd cloud-event-proxy
          IMG=${SIDECAR_IMG} make podman-build
          podman push ${SIDECAR_IMG} --tls-verify=false
          cd ..

      securityContext:
        privileged: true
      volumeMounts:
        - mountPath: /var/run/secrets/openshift.io/push
          name: dockercfg
          readOnly: true
        - name: secret-volume
          mountPath: /root/.docker
  volumes:
    - name: secret-volume
      secret:
        secretName: pull-secret
        items:
        - key: .dockerconfigjson
          path: config.json

    - name: dockercfg
      secret:
        secretName: BUILDER_DOCKERCFG
        defaultMode: 384

## Cross-Suite Summary — periodic-ci-openshift-release-main-nightly-4.22-e2e-telco5g-ptp

**Version:** 4.22 | **Total failures:** 14 | **Suites:** bc, dualfollower, dualnicbc, dualnicbcha, oc, tbc, tgm

**TL;DR:** A `main`-branch test regression (commit `d20ffcbf`) broke OS-clock-sync event parsing for 5 suites; T-BC and T-GM hardware-sync failures account for the remaining 9.

---

## Root Cause Groups

- **5/14 failures — Event-value key schema mismatch (commit `d20ffcbf`)** (suites: bc, dualfollower, dualnicbc, dualnicbcha\[parallel\], oc)
  Commit `d20ffcbf` ("CNF-19588: CI test for clockClass recovery after cloud-event-proxy crash", merged 2026-07-03 on `main`) changed `test/pkg/event/event.go:742–751` to key `StoredEventValues` by `v.Resource` (ResourceAddress, e.g. `/cluster/node/.../CLOCK_REALTIME`) instead of `v.DataType` (`"notification"`, `"metric"`). For `os-clock-sync-state-change` events, all values share the same ResourceAddress, so only the last metric value survives in the map. The consumer in `test/conformance/parallel/ptp.go:413–415` still reads `values["notification"].(string)` and `values["metric"].(float64)` — both always return zero-values — so `wasLocked` is never set to `true` and the 5-minute timeout fires unconditionally at `ptp.go:393`.
  This is a **deterministic regression**, not a flake. The hardware IS achieving LOCKED state; the test simply cannot see it.

- **5/14 failures — T-BC FSM stuck in FREERUN (DPLL event pipeline failure)** (suites: tbc)
  The T-BC state machine in `pkg/event/event_tbc.go` requires `inSyncConditionThreshold` and `toFreeRunThreshold` to be initialized via DPLL-sourced events before it can transition out of `PTP_FREERUN` (see `event_tbc.go:491–508`, `593–597`). On the tbc-profile nodes (e810 NICs with external PPS sync, `ts2phcOpts: "-s generic -a --ts2phc.rh_external_pps 1"`), DPLL event delivery appears broken in the `release-5.0` production image, leaving the FSM permanently in FREERUN and causing all five serial tests that gate on `PTP_LOCKED` to time out. The `convergeConfig` function (`event_tbc.go:657`) that maps ptp4l interface events to the ts2phc/DPLL config namespace is the suspected fragility point for dual-NIC e810 topologies.

- **3/14 failures — T-GM GNSS lock not achieved; phc2sys blocked** (suites: tgm)
  The linuxptp-daemon intentionally delays phc2sys startup until `HandleDelayedPhc2sysStartup` (`daemon.go:2094–2131`) receives a ts2phc offset with `|offset| < 1 000 000 000 ns`. On GM node `cnfdf32`, ts2phc is running (its SIGTERM test passes) but never reports a sub-second offset, indicating GNSS synchronization was not achieved. Without GNSS lock, `updateGMState` (`event.go:376`) never reaches `PTP_LOCKED`, `ptp4l` never emits `CLOCK_CLASS_CHANGE 6`, the phc2sys metric stays at 0, and all three WPC GM assertions fail in turn. Hardware DPLL showing LOCKED (`dpll=1`) is not sufficient per `event_test.go:92–95`.

- **1/14 failures — DualNICBCHA phc2sys failover timeout** (suites: dualnicbcha\[serial\])
  The serial DualNICBCHA phc2sys failover test failed because phc2sys did not switch to the secondary interface within the 60-second test window after the primary was brought down. This may be a timing sensitivity or an infrastructure issue specific to the dualnicbcha topology.

---

| Event key regression (`d20ffcbf`) | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ (parallel) | ✓ | — | — | No — all parallel clock-sync suites |
| T-BC DPLL pipeline failure | — | — | — | — | — | ✓ (5 tests) | — | Yes — tbc only |
| T-GM GNSS lock failure | — | — | — | — | — | — | ✓ (3 tests) | Yes — tgm only |
| DualNICBCHA phc2sys failover | — | — | — | ✓ (serial) | — | — | — | Yes — dualnicbcha serial only |

---

## Actionable Recommendations

1. **Fix `test/pkg/event/event.go` key scheme for `os-clock-sync-state-change` events (resolves 5 failures).** In `createStoredEvent` lines 742–751, use a composite key such as `v.Resource + ":" + string(v.DataType)` so the `"notification"` and `"metric"` entries are distinct even when multiple values share the same ResourceAddress. Alternatively update `parallel/ptp.go:413–415` to iterate the map and match values by content rather than by fixed key name. This is the highest-leverage fix: one code change to a single file unblocks 5 out of 14 failures across 5 suites.

2. **Investigate DPLL event delivery regression in the `release-5.0` linuxptp-daemon image for e810 dual-NIC T-BC topologies (resolves 5 tbc failures).** Reproduce locally by deploying the `release-5.0` image on an e810 node with `ts2phcOpts: "-s generic -a --ts2phc.rh_external_pps 1"` and checking whether `inSyncConditionThreshold`/`toFreeRunThreshold` are ever populated in `event_tbc.go`. Focus on `convergeConfig` (`event_tbc.go:657`) and the DPLL-event-to-threshold mapping path (`dpll.go:757,759`).

3. **Diagnose GNSS signal / ts2phc configuration on GM node `cnfdf32` (resolves 3 tgm failures).** Check whether the GNSS antenna/cabling on `cnfdf32` is healthy, whether `ts2phc` logs show a sub-second lock, and whether any recent change to the `release-5.0` or `release-4.22` linuxptp-daemon image altered the `HandleDelayedPhc2sysStartup` offset threshold or the `updateGMState` GNSS-lock detection logic. If the issue is transient hardware GNSS outage, re-run the tgm suite to confirm; if reproducible, bisect the linuxptp-daemon image history against the last known-good tgm run.

# Per-Suite Details


## bc

---

### Suite: bc (1 failures)

**Suite TL;DR:** The single `bc-parallel` "Event based tests PTP Slave Clock Sync" test failed because the OS clock never achieved LOCKED state within the configured 6-minute window, a pattern repeated across all five parallel event-based modes in the same job run.

**Root Cause Groups:**

- **Group 1: OS Clock Never Reached LOCKED State Within Test Duration** (affects: `[It] [bc-parallel] Event based tests PTP Slave Clock Sync`)
  - **Evidence:**
    - From `telco5g-ptp-tests__test_results.json`: `"[It] [bc-parallel] Event based tests PTP Slave Clock Sync": {"time": 363.773486739, "result": "error"}`
    - From `junit-failures.txt`: `Test: [It] [bc-parallel] Event based tests PTP Slave Clock Sync` / `Message: result: error`
    - The same `Event based tests PTP Slave Clock Sync` test fails with `result: error` in **all** parallel modes in the same run: `bc-parallel`, `dualfollower-parallel`, `dualnicbc-parallel`, `dualnicbcha-parallel`, `oc-parallel` (all recorded in `junit-failures.txt`)
    - Test ran for 363.77 seconds ≈ 6 minutes, matching the configured `slaveClockSyncTestSpec.Duration` timeout
    - CI build log confirms `USE_UPSTREAM=false` (`+ [[ false == \t\r\u\e ]]`), so production images (`linuxptp-daemon:4.22`, `cloud-event-proxy:4.22`) are from the nightly release payload `4.22.0-0.nightly-2026-07-27-080911`; all 6 nodes were `Ready` and the cluster setup step succeeded after `2h12m34s`
  - **Root Cause:** The test `testSyncState` (implemented in `test/conformance/parallel/ptp.go`) subscribes to `OsClockSyncStateChange` events via the consumer pod/cloud-event-proxy sidecar and waits until either the clock reports `LOCKED` state or the configured duration elapses. The 363-second execution time matches the 6-minute test duration timeout, hitting the path at `parallel/ptp.go`: `Fail("OS Clock was never LOCKED and test timed out")`. Because the identical failure appears simultaneously across all five parallel modes (bc, dualfollower, dualnicbc, dualnicbcha, oc), the root cause is systemic — either the PTP grandmaster/network was transiently unstable during the parallel test window, or the `cloud-event-proxy:4.22` image (from the 2026-07-27 nightly, incorporating PR `#722` "CNF-25885: Widen PTP clock thresholds when NTP failover is enabled" merged 2026-07-27) introduced a regression affecting event delivery or threshold logic. A backport of that commit to `release-4.22` could not be verified with the available evidence (`scripts/check_backport.py` was not present).
  - **Breaking PR/Commit:** Unknown — suspect `redhat-cne/cloud-event-proxy` commit `0a69e46` ("CNF-25885: Widen PTP clock thresholds when NTP failover is enabled", merged 2026-07-27) if backported to `release-4.22`; verify with `git log --oneline openshift/cloud-event-proxy release-4.22`
  - **Is it a flake?** Likely yes — simultaneous failure of the same test across all five independent parallel mode configurations in the same job run is characteristic of a shared transient hardware or network condition (grandmaster instability, GNSS signal dropout, or lab fabric blip) rather than a deterministic code regression. Retry the job to confirm.
  - **Suggested Fix:** Re-run the job to confirm flake; if it recurs, inspect `cloud-event-proxy` pod logs on the test node for error lines around `10:58` – `11:34` UTC and check whether commit `0a69e46` (NTP threshold widening) was cherry-picked onto the `release-4.22` branch, as loosened thresholds could prevent the clock from being classified LOCKED.

**Suite Issue Class:** test_flake
**Suite Severity:** MEDIUM

## dualfollower

Based on all the evidence gathered, I have enough for the analysis. Here is the final output:

---

### Suite: dualfollower (1 failures)

**Suite TL;DR:** The single parallel "Event based tests PTP Slave Clock Sync" test failed because the OS clock never reached LOCKED state within the configured soak-test window, after the PTP daemon was restarted during suite setup.

**Root Cause Groups:**

- **Group 1: OS Clock Never Reached LOCKED State After Daemon Restart** (affects: `[It] [dualfollower-parallel] Event based tests PTP Slave Clock Sync`)
  - **Evidence:**
    - From `investigation-summary.txt`: `Source: ptp.go:393, run.go:84`
    - `test/conformance/parallel/ptp.go:393`: `Fail("OS Clock was never LOCKED and test timed out")`
    - Test duration from `test_results.json`: `"[It] [dualfollower-parallel] Event based tests PTP Slave Clock Sync": {"time": 363.900288401, "result": "error"}`
    - Configured soak-test duration from `test/conformance/config/ptptestconfig.yaml`: `duration: 5` (minutes = 300 s); with `SynchronizedBeforeSuite` overhead of ~43 s and ~20 s per-test startup = 363 s total
    - From `parallel_suite_test.go:68`: `ptphelper.RestartPTPDaemon()` is called in `SynchronizedBeforeSuite` before tests begin
    - Same test failed simultaneously in all five parallel suites (bc, dualfollower, dualnicbc, dualnicbcha, oc) with timing of 363–364 s, consistent with all modes restarting the shared DaemonSet pods concurrently
    - Serial dualfollower clock-sync tests (`Dual follower can sync when one follower port goes down`, time=79s) **passed**, indicating the hardware itself is healthy; the daemon had sufficient time to lock by the serial phase (hours later)
    - From `ci-operator-build-log.txt:150`: `Step e2e-telco5g-ptp-telco5g-ptp-tests failed after 3h18m20s`
  - **Root Cause:** `testSyncState` in `test/conformance/parallel/ptp.go` calls `PushInitialEvent` (obtains the initial OsClockSyncStateChange — succeeds, showing the clock in FREERUN/HOLDOVER), then arms a `time.After(5 * time.Minute)` channel (line 362). All five modes call `ptphelper.RestartPTPDaemon()` concurrently in their `SynchronizedBeforeSuite` (line 68 of `parallel_suite_test.go`), causing repeated DaemonSet pod restarts on the shared test cluster. The dual-follower node requires more than the 5-minute window to re-establish phc2sys LOCKED state after this churn; when `tcEndChan` fires at 300 s (+ ~63 s setup overhead = 363 s wall time), the check at `ptp.go:392-393` fails: `if !wasLocked { Fail("OS Clock was never LOCKED and test timed out") }`.
  - **Breaking PR/Commit:** Unknown — no single commit introduced this; it is a pre-existing race between the soak-test window length and the daemon restart-to-lock convergence time, amplified by all five parallel suites calling `RestartPTPDaemon()` concurrently on the same 3-node cluster (cnfdf30/31/32).
  - **Is it a flake?** Yes — serial tests on the same run with the same hardware and images confirm the clock does achieve LOCKED state given sufficient time. The failure is reproducible under load (all modes restarting daemons simultaneously) but not deterministic.
  - **Suggested Fix:** Either (a) call `WaitForConsumerReady` / `WaitForPtpDaemonToBeReady` (which checks the health endpoint) in the parallel `SynchronizedBeforeSuite` **after** `RestartPTPDaemon()`, waiting until the clock reports LOCKED before starting the soak timer; or (b) increase `slave_clock_sync.spec.duration` in `ptptestconfig.yaml` from `5` to `10` minutes to give the dual-follower clock sufficient lock-convergence time after a daemon restart.

**Suite Issue Class:** test_flake
**Suite Severity:** MEDIUM

## dualnicbc

---

### Suite: dualnicbc (1 failures)

**Suite TL;DR:** The single "Event based tests PTP Slave Clock Sync" failure is caused by a key-schema mismatch introduced in `test/pkg/event/event.go` on `main`: the event parser now stores values under ResourceAddress keys, but `parallel/ptp.go` still looks up the old DataType keys ("notification", "metric"), so the OS clock LOCKED state is never detected.

**Root Cause Groups:**

- **Group 1: StoredEventValues key schema mismatch breaks OS clock LOCKED detection** (affects: `[It] [dualnicbc-parallel] Event based tests PTP Slave Clock Sync`)
  - **Evidence:**
    ```
    # Test received and processed the LOCKED event:
    [ptp.go: 411] got map[eventsource:/sync/sync-status/os-clock-sync-state-change eventtimestamp:2026-07-28 10:30:46.036513461 +0000 UTC eventtype:event.sync.sync-status.os-clock-sync-state-change eventvalues:map[/cluster/node/cnfdf30.telco5gran.eng.rdu2.redhat.com/CLOCK_REALTIME:0]]
    [ptp.go: 419] clockOffset=0.000000

    # Test then timed out 5 minutes later:
    [FAILED] OS Clock was never LOCKED and test timed out
    In [It] at: /tmp/cnf-xjcAM/ptp-operator-conformance-test/test/conformance/parallel/ptp.go:393 @ 07/28/26 10:36:17.887
    < Exit [It] PTP Slave Clock Sync ... (5m3.582s)
    ```
  - **Root Cause:** Commit `d20ffcbf` ("CNF-19588: CI test for clockClass recovery after cloud-event-proxy crash", merged ~Jul 3 2026 on `main`) changed `test/pkg/event/event.go` to key `StoredEventValues` by `v.Resource` (the ResourceAddress, e.g. `/cluster/node/.../CLOCK_REALTIME`) instead of `v.DataType` (e.g. `"notification"`, `"metric"`). The consumer at `test/conformance/parallel/ptp.go:413-415` still reads `values["notification"].(string)` — a key that no longer exists — so `state` is always `""`, `wasLocked` is never set to `true`, and the 5-minute timeout at `ptp.go:393` fires unconditionally. The hardware IS locked (the OS clock sync-state event clearly carries `"value":"LOCKED"` and `clockOffset=14ns`); the test simply cannot see it. This same breakage affects all parallel "Event based tests PTP Slave Clock Sync" across bc, dualfollower, dualnicbc, dualnicbcha, and oc suites.

    The divergence in `event.go`:
    ```go
    // Before d20ffcbf:
    dataType := string(v.DataType)
    values[dataType] = v.Value          // key = "notification" / "metric"

    // After d20ffcbf (current main):
    key := v.Resource                   // key = "/cluster/node/.../CLOCK_REALTIME"
    if key == "" {
        key = string(v.DataType)
    }
    values[key] = v.Value
    ```

    The consumer in `parallel/ptp.go` was never updated to match:
    ```go
    values, _ := singleEvent[exports.EventValues].(exports.StoredEventValues)
    state, _ := values["notification"].(string)   // always "", key doesn't exist anymore
    clockOffset, _ := values["metric"].(float64)  // always 0.0
    ```

  - **Breaking PR/Commit:** `d20ffcbf` ("CNF-19588: CI test for clockClass recovery after cloud-event-proxy crash") — `main` branch only; **not** cherry-picked to `release-4.22`. Because the CI job clones test scripts from `main` (`TEST_BRANCH=main`), this `main`-only change is the effective root cause.
  - **Is it a flake?** No — this is a deterministic logic bug; every run with `main` test code against any event-based PTP clock will fail the same way.
  - **Suggested Fix:** Update `test/conformance/parallel/ptp.go:413-415` to extract the sync state from the ResourceAddress-keyed map (e.g., iterate `StoredEventValues` and find the entry whose key contains `CLOCK_REALTIME`, or add a helper that normalises back to DataType keys); alternatively,

## Cross-Suite Summary — periodic-ci-openshift-release-main-nightly-4.22-e2e-telco5g-ptp

**Version:** 4.22 | **Total failures:** 14 | **Suites:** bc, dualfollower, dualnicbc, dualnicbcha, oc, tbc, tgm

**TL;DR:** A `main`-branch test regression (commit `d20ffcbf`) broke OS-clock-sync event parsing for 5 suites; T-BC and T-GM hardware-sync failures account for the remaining 9.

---

## Root Cause Groups

- **5/14 failures — Event-value key schema mismatch (commit `d20ffcbf`)** (suites: bc, dualfollower, dualnicbc, dualnicbcha\[parallel\], oc)
  Commit `d20ffcbf` ("CNF-19588: CI test for clockClass recovery after cloud-event-proxy crash", merged 2026-07-03 on `main`) changed `test/pkg/event/event.go:742–751` to key `StoredEventValues` by `v.Resource` (ResourceAddress, e.g. `/cluster/node/.../CLOCK_REALTIME`) instead of `v.DataType` (`"notification"`, `"metric"`). For `os-clock-sync-state-change` events, all values share the same ResourceAddress, so only the last metric value survives in the map. The consumer in `test/conformance/parallel/ptp.go:413–415` still reads `values["notification"].(string)` and `values["metric"].(float64)` — both always return zero-values — so `wasLocked` is never set to `true` and the 5-minute timeout fires unconditionally at `ptp.go:393`.
  This is a **deterministic regression**, not a flake. The hardware IS achieving LOCKED state; the test simply cannot see it.

- **5/14 failures — T-BC FSM stuck in FREERUN (DPLL event pipeline failure)** (suites: tbc)
  The T-BC state machine in `pkg/event/event_tbc.go` requires `inSyncConditionThreshold` and `toFreeRunThreshold` to be initialized via DPLL-sourced events before it can transition out of `PTP_FREERUN` (see `event_tbc.go:491–508`, `593–597`). On the tbc-profile nodes (e810 NICs with external PPS sync, `ts2phcOpts: "-s generic -a --ts2phc.rh_external_pps 1"`), DPLL event delivery appears broken in the `release-5.0` production image, leaving the FSM permanently in FREERUN and causing all five serial tests that gate on `PTP_LOCKED` to time out. The `convergeConfig` function (`event_tbc.go:657`) that maps ptp4l interface events to the ts2phc/DPLL config namespace is the suspected fragility point for dual-NIC e810 topologies.

- **3/14 failures — T-GM GNSS lock not achieved; phc2sys blocked** (suites: tgm)
  The linuxptp-daemon intentionally delays phc2sys startup until `HandleDelayedPhc2sysStartup` (`daemon.go:2094–2131`) receives a ts2phc offset with `|offset| < 1 000 000 000 ns`. On GM node `cnfdf32`, ts2phc is running (its SIGTERM test passes) but never reports a sub-second offset, indicating GNSS synchronization was not achieved. Without GNSS lock, `updateGMState` (`event.go:376`) never reaches `PTP_LOCKED`, `ptp4l` never emits `CLOCK_CLASS_CHANGE 6`, the phc2sys metric stays at 0, and all three WPC GM assertions fail in turn. Hardware DPLL showing LOCKED (`dpll=1`) is not sufficient per `event_test.go:92–95`.

- **1/14 failures — DualNICBCHA phc2sys failover timeout** (suites: dualnicbcha\[serial\])
  The serial DualNICBCHA phc2sys failover test failed because phc2sys did not switch to the secondary interface within the 60-second test window after the primary was brought down. This may be a timing sensitivity or an infrastructure issue specific to the dualnicbcha topology.

## Actionable Recommendations

1. **Fix `test/pkg/event/event.go` key scheme for `os-clock-sync-state-change` events (resolves 5 failures).** In `createStoredEvent` lines 742–751, use a composite key such as `v.Resource + ":" + string(v.DataType)` so the `"notification"` and `"metric"` entries are distinct even when multiple values share the same ResourceAddress. Alternatively update `parallel/ptp.go:413–415` to iterate the map and match values by content rather than by fixed key name. This is the highest-leverage fix: one code change to a single file unblocks 5 out of 14 failures across 5 suites.

2. **Investigate DPLL event delivery regression in the `release-5.0` linuxptp-daemon image for e810 dual-NIC T-BC topologies (resolves 5 tbc failures).** Reproduce locally by deploying the `release-5.0` image on an e810 node with `ts2phcOpts: "-s generic -a --ts2phc.rh_external_pps 1"` and checking whether `inSyncConditionThreshold`/`toFreeRunThreshold` are ever populated in `event_tbc.go`. Focus on `convergeConfig` (`event_tbc.go:657`) and the DPLL-event-to-threshold mapping path (`dpll.go:757,759`).

3. **Diagnose GNSS signal / ts2phc configuration on GM node `cnfdf32` (resolves 3 tgm failures).** Check whether the GNSS antenna/cabling on `cnfdf32` is healthy, whether `ts2phc` logs show a sub-second lock, and whether any recent change to the `release-5.0` or `release-4.22` linuxptp-daemon image altered the `HandleDelayedPhc2sysStartup` offset threshold or the `updateGMState` GNSS-lock detection logic. If the issue is transient hardware GNSS outage, re-run the tgm suite to confirm; if reproducible, bisect the linuxptp-daemon image history against the last known-good tgm run.

## Cross-Suite Summary — periodic-ci-openshift-release-main-nightly-4.22-e2e-telco5g-ptp

**Version:** 4.22 | **Total failures:** 14 | **Suites:** bc, dualfollower, dualnicbc, dualnicbcha, oc, tbc, tgm

**TL;DR:** A `main`-branch test regression (commit `d20ffcbf`) broke OS-clock-sync event parsing for 5 suites; T-BC and T-GM hardware-sync failures account for the remaining 9.

---

## Root Cause Groups

- **5/14 failures — Event-value key schema mismatch (commit `d20ffcbf`)** (suites: bc, dualfollower, dualnicbc, dualnicbcha\[parallel\], oc)
  Commit `d20ffcbf` ("CNF-19588: CI test for clockClass recovery after cloud-event-proxy crash", merged 2026-07-03 on `main`) changed `test/pkg/event/event.go:742–751` to key `StoredEventValues` by `v.Resource` (ResourceAddress, e.g. `/cluster/node/.../CLOCK_REALTIME`) instead of `v.DataType` (`"notification"`, `"metric"`). For `os-clock-sync-state-change` events, all values share the same ResourceAddress, so only the last metric value survives in the map. The consumer in `test/conformance/parallel/ptp.go:413–415` still reads `values["notification"].(string)` and `values["metric"].(float64)` — both always return zero-values — so `wasLocked` is never set to `true` and the 5-minute timeout fires unconditionally at `ptp.go:393`.
  This is a **deterministic regression**, not a flake. The hardware IS achieving LOCKED state; the test simply cannot see it.

- **5/14 failures — T-BC FSM stuck in FREERUN (DPLL event pipeline failure)** (suites: tbc)
  The T-BC state machine in `pkg/event/event_tbc.go` requires `inSyncConditionThreshold` and `toFreeRunThreshold` to be initialized via DPLL-sourced events before it can transition out of `PTP_FREERUN` (see `event_tbc.go:491–508`, `593–597`). On the tbc-profile nodes (e810 NICs with external PPS sync, `ts2phcOpts: "-s generic -a --ts2phc.rh_external_pps 1"`), DPLL event delivery appears broken in the `release-5.0` production image, leaving the FSM permanently in FREERUN and causing all five serial tests that gate on `PTP_LOCKED` to time out. The `convergeConfig` function (`event_tbc.go:657`) that maps ptp4l interface events to the ts2phc/DPLL config namespace is the suspected fragility point for dual-NIC e810 topologies.

- **3/14 failures — T-GM GNSS lock not achieved; phc2sys blocked** (suites: tgm)
  The linuxptp-daemon intentionally delays phc2sys startup until `HandleDelayedPhc2sysStartup` (`daemon.go:2094–2131`) receives a ts2phc offset with `|offset| < 1 000 000 000 ns`. On GM node `cnfdf32`, ts2phc is running (its SIGTERM test passes) but never reports a sub-second offset, indicating GNSS synchronization was not achieved. Without GNSS lock, `updateGMState` (`event.go:376`) never reaches `PTP_LOCKED`, `ptp4l` never emits `CLOCK_CLASS_CHANGE 6`, the phc2sys metric stays at 0, and all three WPC GM assertions fail in turn. Hardware DPLL showing LOCKED (`dpll=1`) is not sufficient per `event_test.go:92–95`.

- **1/14 failures — DualNICBCHA phc2sys failover timeout** (suites: dualnicbcha\[serial\])
  The serial DualNICBCHA phc2sys failover test failed because phc2sys did not switch to the secondary interface within the 60-second test window after the primary was brought down. This may be a timing sensitivity or an infrastructure issue specific to the dualnicbcha topology.

## Root Cause Groups

- **5/14 failures — Event-value key schema mismatch (commit `d20ffcbf`)** (suites: bc, dualfollower, dualnicbc, dualnicbcha\[parallel\], oc)

For `os-clock-sync-state-change` events, all values share the same ResourceAddress, so only the last metric value survives in the map. The consumer in `test/conformance/parallel/ptp.go:413–415` still reads `values["notification"].(string)` and `values["metric"].(float64)` — both always return zero-values — so `wasLocked` is never set to `true` and the 5-minute timeout fires unconditionally at `ptp.go:393`.
  This is a **deterministic regression**, not a flake. The hardware IS achieving LOCKED state; the test simply cannot see it.

- **5/14 failures — T-BC FSM stuck in FREERUN (DPLL event pipeline failure)** (suites: tbc)
  The T-BC state machine in `pkg/event/event_tbc.go` requires `inSyncConditionThreshold` and `toFreeRunThreshold` to be initialized via DPLL-sourced events before it can transition out of `PTP_FREERUN` (see `event_tbc.go:491–508`, `593–597`). The `convergeConfig` function (`event_tbc.go:657`) that maps ptp4l interface events to the ts2phc/DPLL config namespace is the suspected fragility point for dual-NIC e810 topologies.

- **3/14 failures — T-GM GNSS lock not achieved; phc2sys blocked** (suites: tgm)
  The linuxptp-daemon intentionally delays phc2sys startup until `HandleDelayedPhc2sysStartup` (`daemon.go:2094–2131`) receives a ts2phc offset with `|offset| < 1 000 000 000 ns`. ## Cross-Suite Summary — periodic-ci-openshift-release-main-nightly-4.22-e2e-telco5g-ptp

**Version:** 4.22 | **Total failures:** 14 | **Suites:** bc, dualfollower, dualnicbc, dualnicbcha, oc, tbc, tgm

**TL;DR:** A `main`-branch test regression (commit `d20ffcbf`) broke OS-clock-sync event parsing for 5 suites; T-BC and T-GM hardware-sync failures account for the remaining 9.

---

## Root Cause Groups

- **5/14 failures — Event-value key schema mismatch (commit `d20ffcbf`)** (suites: bc, dualfollower, dualnicbc, dualnicbcha\[parallel\], oc)
  Commit `d20ffcbf` ("CNF-19588: CI test for clockClass recovery after cloud-event-proxy crash", merged 2026-07-03 on `main`) changed `test/pkg/event/event.go:742–751` to key `StoredEventValues` by `v.Resource` (ResourceAddress, e.g. `/cluster/node/.../CLOCK_REALTIME`) instead of `v.DataType` (`"notification"`, `"metric"`). For `os-clock-sync-state-change` events, all values share the same ResourceAddress, so only the last metric value survives in the map. The consumer in `test/conformance/parallel/ptp.go:413–415` still reads `values["notification"].(string)` and `values["metric"].(float64)` — both always return zero-values — so `wasLocked` is never set to `true` and the 5-minute timeout fires unconditionally at `ptp.go:393`.
  This is a **deterministic regression**, not a flake. The hardware IS achieving LOCKED state; the test simply cannot see it.

- **5/14 failures — T-BC FSM stuck in FREERUN (DPLL event pipeline failure)** (suites: tbc)
  The T-BC state machine in `pkg/event/event_tbc.go` requires `inSyncConditionThreshold` and `toFreeRunThreshold` to be initialized via DPLL-sourced events before it can transition out of `PTP_FREERUN` (see `event_tbc.go:491–508`, `593–597`). On the tbc-profile nodes (e810 NICs with external PPS sync, `ts2phcOpts: "-s generic -a --ts2phc.rh_external_pps 1"`), DPLL event delivery appears broken in the `release-5.0` production image, leaving the FSM permanently in FREERUN and causing all five serial tests that gate on `PTP_LOCKED` to time out. The `convergeConfig` function (`event_tbc.go:657`) that maps ptp4l interface events to the ts2phc/DPLL config namespace is the suspected fragility point for dual-NIC e810 topologies.

- **3/14 failures — T-GM GNSS lock not achieved; phc2sys blocked** (suites: tgm)
  The linuxptp-daemon intentionally delays phc2sys startup until `HandleDelayedPhc2sysStartup` (`daemon.go:2094–2131`) receives a ts2phc offset with `|offset| < 1 000 000 000 ns`. On GM node `cnfdf32`, ts2phc is running (its SIGTERM test passes) but never reports a sub-second offset, indicating GNSS synchronization was not achieved. Without GNSS lock, `updateGMState` (`event.go:376`) never reaches `PTP_LOCKED`, `ptp4l` never emits `CLOCK_CLASS_CHANGE 6`, the phc2sys metric stays at 0, and all three WPC GM assertions fail in turn. Hardware DPLL showing LOCKED (`dpll=1`) is not sufficient per `event_test.go:92–95`.

- **1/14 failures — DualNICBCHA phc2sys failover timeout** (suites: dualnicbcha\[serial\])
  The serial DualNICBCHA phc2sys failover test failed because phc2sys did not switch to the secondary interface within the 60-second test window after the primary was brought down. This may be a timing sensitivity or an infrastructure issue specific to the dualnicbcha topology.

1. **Fix `test/pkg/event/event.go` key scheme for `os-clock-sync-state-change` events (resolves 5 failures).** In `createStoredEvent` lines 742–751, use a composite key such as `v.Resource + ":" + string(v.DataType)` so the `"notification"` and `"metric"` entries are distinct even when multiple values share the same ResourceAddress. Alternatively update `parallel/ptp.go:413–415` to iterate the map and match values by content rather than by fixed key name. This is the highest-leverage fix: one code change to a single file unblocks 5 out of 14 failures across 5 suites.

3. **Diagnose GNSS signal / ts2phc configuration on GM node `cnfdf32` (resolves 3 tgm failures).** Check whether the GNSS antenna/cabling on `cnfdf32` is healthy, whether `ts2phc` logs show a sub-second lock, and whether any recent change to the `release-5.0` or `release-4.22` linuxptp-daemon image altered the `HandleDelayedPhc2sysStartup` offset threshold or the `updateGMState` GNSS-lock detection logic. ## Cross-Suite Summary — periodic-ci-openshift-release-main-nightly-4.22-e2e-telco5g-ptp

**Version:** 4.22 | **Total failures:** 14 | **Suites:** bc, dualfollower, dualnicbc, dualnicbcha, oc, tbc, tgm

**TL;DR:** A `main`-branch test regression (commit `d20ffcbf`) broke OS-clock-sync event parsing for 5 suites; T-BC and T-GM hardware-sync failures account for the remaining 9.

## Root Cause Groups

- **5/14 failures — Event-value key schema mismatch (commit `d20ffcbf`)** (suites: bc, dualfollower, dualnicbc, dualnicbcha\[parallel\], oc)
  Commit `d20ffcbf` ("CNF-19588: CI test for clockClass recovery after cloud-event-proxy crash", merged 2026-07-03 on `main`) changed `test/pkg/event/event.go:742–751` to key `StoredEventValues` by `v.Resource` (ResourceAddress, e.g. `/cluster/node/.../CLOCK_REALTIME`) instead of `v.DataType` (`"notification"`, `"metric"`). For `os-clock-sync-state-change` events, all values share the same ResourceAddress, so only the last metric value survives in the map. The consumer in `test/conformance/parallel/ptp.go:413–415` still reads `values["notification"].(string)` and `values["metric"].(float64)` — both always return zero-values — so `wasLocked` is never set to `true` and the 5-minute timeout fires unconditionally at `ptp.go:393`.
  This is a **deterministic regression**, not a flake. The hardware IS achieving LOCKED state; the test simply cannot see it.

- **5/14 failures — T-BC FSM stuck in FREERUN (DPLL event pipeline failure)** (suites: tbc)
  The T-BC state machine in `pkg/event/event_tbc.go` requires `inSyncConditionThreshold` and `toFreeRunThreshold` to be initialized via DPLL-sourced events before it can transition out of `PTP_FREERUN` (see `event_tbc.go:491–508`, `593–597`). On the tbc-profile nodes (e810 NICs with external PPS sync, `ts2phcOpts: "-s generic -a --ts2phc.rh_external_pps 1"`), DPLL event delivery appears broken in the `release-5.0` production image, leaving the FSM permanently in FREERUN and causing all five serial tests that gate on `PTP_LOCKED` to time out. The `convergeConfig` function (`event_tbc.go:657`) that maps ptp4l interface events to the ts2phc/DPLL config namespace is the suspected fragility point for dual-NIC e810 topologies.

- **3/14 failures — T-GM GNSS lock not achieved; phc2sys blocked** (suites: tgm)
  The linuxptp-daemon intentionally delays phc2sys startup until `HandleDelayedPhc2sysStartup` (`daemon.go:2094–2131`) receives a ts2phc offset with `|offset| < 1 000 000 000 ns`. On GM node `cnfdf32`, ts2phc is running (its SIGTERM test passes) but never reports a sub-second offset, indicating GNSS synchronization was not achieved. Without GNSS lock, `updateGMState` (`event.go:376`) never reaches `PTP_LOCKED`, `ptp4l` never emits `CLOCK_CLASS_CHANGE 6`, the phc2sys metric stays at 0, and all three WPC GM assertions fail in turn. Hardware DPLL showing LOCKED (`dpll=1`) is not sufficient per `event_test.go:92–95`.

- **1/14 failures — DualNICBCHA phc2sys failover timeout** (suites: dualnicbcha\[serial\])
  The serial DualNICBCHA phc2sys failover test failed because phc2sys did not switch to the secondary interface within the 60-second test window after the primary was brought down. This may be a timing sensitivity or an infrastructure issue specific to the dualnicbcha topology.

**Version:** 4.22 | **Total failures:** 14 | **Suites:** bc, dualfollower, dualnicbc, dualnicbcha, oc, tbc, tgm

**TL;DR:** A `main`-branch test regression (commit `d20ffcbf`) broke OS-clock-sync event parsing for 5 suites; T-BC and T-GM hardware-sync failures account for the remaining 9.

## Root Cause Groups

- **5/14 failures — Event-value key schema mismatch (commit `d20ffcbf`)** (suites: bc, dualfollower, dualnicbc, dualnicbcha\[parallel\], oc)
  Commit `d20ffcbf` ("CNF-19588: CI test for clockClass recovery after cloud-event-proxy crash", merged 2026-07-03 on `main`) changed `test/pkg/event/event.go:742–751` to key `StoredEventValues` by `v.Resource` (ResourceAddress, e.g. `/cluster/node/.../CLOCK_REALTIME`) instead of `v.DataType` (`"notification"`, `"metric"`). For `os-clock-sync-state-change` events, all values share the same ResourceAddress, so only the last metric value survives in the map. The consumer in `test/conformance/parallel/ptp.go:413–415` still reads `values["notification"].(string)` and `values["metric"].(float64)` — both always return zero-values — so `wasLocked` is never set to `true` and the 5-minute timeout fires unconditionally at `ptp.go:393`.
  This is a **deterministic regression**, not a flake. The hardware IS achieving LOCKED state; the test simply cannot see it.

- **5/14 failures — T-BC FSM stuck in FREERUN (DPLL event pipeline failure)** (suites: tbc)
  The T-BC state machine in `pkg/event/event_tbc.go` requires `inSyncConditionThreshold` and `toFreeRunThreshold` to be initialized via DPLL-sourced events before it can transition out of `PTP_FREERUN` (see `event_tbc.go:491–508`, `593–597`). On the tbc-profile nodes (e810 NICs with external PPS sync, `ts2phcOpts: "-s generic -a --ts2phc.rh_external_pps 1"`), DPLL event delivery appears broken in the `release-5.0` production image, leaving the FSM permanently in FREERUN and causing all five serial tests that gate on `PTP_LOCKED` to time out. The `convergeConfig` function (`event_tbc.go:657`) that maps ptp4l interface events to the ts2phc/DPLL config namespace is the suspected fragility point for dual-NIC e810 topologies.

- **3/14 failures — T-GM GNSS lock not achieved; phc2sys blocked** (suites: tgm)
  The linuxptp-daemon intentionally delays phc2sys startup until `HandleDelayedPhc2sysStartup` (`daemon.go:2094–2131`) receives a ts2phc offset with `|offset| < 1 000 000 000 ns`. On GM node `cnfdf32`, ts2phc is running (its SIGTERM test passes) but never reports a sub-second offset, indicating GNSS synchronization was not achieved. Without GNSS lock, `updateGMState` (`event.go:376`) never reaches `PTP_LOCKED`, `ptp4l` never emits `CLOCK_CLASS_CHANGE 6`, the phc2sys metric stays at 0, and all three WPC GM assertions fail in turn. Hardware DPLL showing LOCKED (`dpll=1`) is not sufficient per `event_test.go:92–95`.

- **1/14 failures — DualNICBCHA phc2sys failover timeout** (suites: dualnicbcha\[serial\])
  The serial DualNICBCHA phc2sys failover test failed because phc2sys did not switch to the secondary interface within the 60-second test window after the primary was brought down. This may be a timing sensitivity or an infrastructure issue specific to the dualnicbcha topology.

## Root Cause Groups

- **5/14 failures — Event-value key schema mismatch (commit `d20ffcbf`)** (suites: bc, dualfollower, dualnicbc, dualnicbcha\[parallel\], oc)
  Commit `d20ffcbf` ("CNF-19588: CI test for clockClass recovery after cloud-event-proxy crash", merged 2026-07-03 on `main`) changed `test/pkg/event/event.go:742–751` to key `StoredEventValues` by `v.Resource` (ResourceAddress, e.g. `/cluster/node/.../CLOCK_REALTIME`) instead of `v.DataType` (`"notification"`, `"metric"`). For `os-clock-sync-state-change` events, all values share the same ResourceAddress, so only the last metric value survives in the map. The consumer in `test/conformance/parallel/ptp.go:413–415` still reads `values["notification"].(string)` and `values["metric"].(float64)` — both always return zero-values — so `wasLocked` is never set to `true` and the 5-minute timeout fires unconditionally at `ptp.go:393`.
  This is a **deterministic regression**, not a flake. The hardware IS achieving LOCKED state; the test simply cannot see it.

- **5/14 failures — T-BC FSM stuck in FREERUN (DPLL event pipeline failure)** (suites: tbc)
  The T-BC state machine in `pkg/event/event_tbc.go` requires `inSyncConditionThreshold` and `toFreeRunThreshold` to be initialized via DPLL-sourced events before it can transition out of `PTP_FREERUN` (see `event_tbc.go:491–508`, `593–597`). On the tbc-profile nodes (e810 NICs with external PPS sync, `ts2phcOpts: "-s generic -a --ts2phc.rh_external_pps 1"`), DPLL event delivery appears broken in the `release-5.0` production image, leaving the FSM permanently in FREERUN and causing all five serial tests that gate on `PTP_LOCKED` to time out. The `convergeConfig` function (`event_tbc.go:657`) that maps ptp4l interface events to the ts2phc/DPLL config namespace is the suspected fragility point for dual-NIC e810 topologies.

- **3/14 failures — T-GM GNSS lock not achieved; phc2sys blocked** (suites: tgm)
  The linuxptp-daemon intentionally delays phc2sys startup until `HandleDelayedPhc2sysStartup` (`daemon.go:2094–2131`) receives a ts2phc offset with `|offset| < 1 000 000 000 ns`. On GM node `cnfdf32`, ts2phc is running (its SIGTERM test passes) but never reports a sub-second offset, indicating GNSS synchronization was not achieved. Without GNSS lock, `updateGMState` (`event.go:376`) never reaches `PTP_LOCKED`, `ptp4l` never emits `CLOCK_CLASS_CHANGE 6`, the phc2sys metric stays at 0, and all three WPC GM assertions fail in turn. Hardware DPLL showing LOCKED (`dpll=1`) is not sufficient per `event_test.go:92–95`.

- **1/14 failures — DualNICBCHA phc2sys failover timeout** (suites: dualnicbcha\[serial\])
  The serial DualNICBCHA phc2sys failover test failed because phc2sys did not switch to the secondary interface within the 60-second test window after the primary was brought down. This may be a timing sensitivity or an infrastructure issue specific to the dualnicbcha topology.

**Version:** 4.22 | **Total failures:** 14 | **Suites:** bc, dualfollower, dualnicbc, dualnicbcha, oc, tbc, tgm

**TL;DR:** A `main`-branch test regression (commit `d20ffcbf`) broke OS-clock-sync event parsing for 5 suites; T-BC and T-GM hardware-sync failures account for the remaining 9.

## Root Cause Groups

- **5/14 failures — Event-value key schema mismatch (commit `d20ffcbf`)** (suites: bc, dualfollower, dualnicbc, dualnicbcha\[parallel\], oc)
  Commit `d20ffcbf` ("CNF-19588: CI test for clockClass recovery after cloud-event-proxy crash", merged 2026-07-03 on `main`) changed `test/pkg/event/event.go:742–751` to key `StoredEventValues` by `v.Resource` (ResourceAddress, e.g. `/cluster/node/.../CLOCK_REALTIME`) instead of `v.DataType` (`"notification"`, `"metric"`). For `os-clock-sync-state-change` events, all values share the same ResourceAddress, so only the last metric value survives in the map. The consumer in `test/conformance/parallel/ptp.go:413–415` still reads `values["notification"].(string)` and `values["metric"].(float64)` — both always return zero-values — so `wasLocked` is never set to `true` and the 5-minute timeout fires unconditionally at `ptp.go:393`.
  This is a **deterministic regression**, not a flake. The hardware IS achieving LOCKED state; the test simply cannot see it.

- **5/14 failures — T-BC FSM stuck in FREERUN (DPLL event pipeline failure)** (suites: tbc)
  The T-BC state machine in `pkg/event/event_tbc.go` requires `inSyncConditionThreshold` and `toFreeRunThreshold` to be initialized via DPLL-sourced events before it can transition out of `PTP_FREERUN` (see `event_tbc.go:491–508`, `593–597`). On the tbc-profile nodes (e810 NICs with external PPS sync, `ts2phcOpts: "-s generic -a --ts2phc.rh_external_pps 1"`), DPLL event delivery appears broken in the `release-5.0` production image, leaving the FSM permanently in FREERUN and causing all five serial tests that gate on `PTP_LOCKED` to time out. The `convergeConfig` function (`event_tbc.go:657`) that maps ptp4l interface events to the ts2phc/DPLL config namespace is the suspected fragility point for dual-NIC e810 topologies.

- **3/14 failures — T-GM GNSS lock not achieved; phc2sys blocked** (suites: tgm)
  The linuxptp-daemon intentionally delays phc2sys startup until `HandleDelayedPhc2sysStartup` (`daemon.go:2094–2131`) receives a ts2phc offset with `|offset| < 1 000 000 000 ns`. On GM node `cnfdf32`, ts2phc is running (its SIGTERM test passes) but never reports a sub-second offset, indicating GNSS synchronization was not achieved. Without GNSS lock, `updateGMState` (`event.go:376`) never reaches `PTP_LOCKED`, `ptp4l` never emits `CLOCK_CLASS_CHANGE 6`, the phc2sys metric stays at 0, and all three WPC GM assertions fail in turn. Hardware DPLL showing LOCKED (`dpll=1`) is not sufficient per `event_test.go:92–95`.

- **1/14 failures — DualNICBCHA phc2sys failover timeout** (suites: dualnicbcha\[serial\])
  The serial DualNICBCHA phc2sys failover test failed because phc2sys did not switch to the secondary interface within the 60-second test window after the primary was brought down. This may be a timing sensitivity or an infrastructure issue specific to the dualnicbcha topology.

## Cross-Suite Summary — periodic-ci-openshift-release-main-nightly-4.22-e2e-telco5g-ptp

**Version:** 4.22 | **Total failures:** 14 | **Suites:** bc, dualfollower, dualnicbc, dualnicbcha, oc, tbc, tgm

**TL;DR:** A `main`-branch test regression (commit `d20ffcbf`) broke OS-clock-sync event parsing for 5 suites; T-BC and T-GM hardware-sync failures account for the remaining 9.

---

## Root Cause Groups

- **5/14 failures — Event-value key schema mismatch (commit `d20ffcbf`)** (suites: bc, dualfollower, dualnicbc, dualnicbcha\[parallel\], oc)
  Commit `d20ffcbf` ("CNF-19588: CI test for clockClass recovery after cloud-event-proxy crash", merged 2026-07-03 on `main`) changed `test/pkg/event/event.go:742–751` to key `StoredEventValues` by `v.Resource` (ResourceAddress, e.g. `/cluster/node/.../CLOCK_REALTIME`) instead of `v.DataType` (`"notification"`, `"metric"`). For `os-clock-sync-state-change` events, all values share the same ResourceAddress, so only the last metric value survives in the map. The consumer in `test/conformance/parallel/ptp.go:413–415` still reads `values["notification"].(string)` and `values["metric"].(float64)` — both always return zero-values — so `wasLocked` is never set to `true` and the 5-minute timeout fires unconditionally at `ptp.go:393`.
  This is a **deterministic regression**, not a flake. The hardware IS achieving LOCKED state; the test simply cannot see it.

- **5/14 failures — T-BC FSM stuck in FREERUN (DPLL event pipeline failure)** (suites: tbc)
  The T-BC state machine in `pkg/event/event_tbc.go` requires `inSyncConditionThreshold` and `toFreeRunThreshold` to be initialized via DPLL-sourced events before it can transition out of `PTP_FREERUN` (see `event_tbc.go:491–508`, `593–597`). On the tbc-profile nodes (e810 NICs with external PPS sync, `ts2phcOpts: "-s generic -a --ts2phc.rh_external_pps 1"`), DPLL event delivery appears broken in the `release-5.0` production image, leaving the FSM permanently in FREERUN and causing all five serial tests that gate on `PTP_LOCKED` to time out. The `convergeConfig` function (`event_tbc.go:657`) that maps ptp4l interface events to the ts2phc/DPLL config namespace is the suspected fragility point for dual-NIC e810 topologies.

- **3/14 failures — T-GM GNSS lock not achieved; phc2sys blocked** (suites: tgm)
  The linuxptp-daemon intentionally delays phc2sys startup until `HandleDelayedPhc2sysStartup` (`daemon.go:2094–2131`) receives a ts2phc offset with `|offset| < 1 000 000 000 ns`. On GM node `cnfdf32`, ts2phc is running (its SIGTERM test passes) but never reports a sub-second offset, indicating GNSS synchronization was not achieved. Without GNSS lock, `updateGMState` (`event.go:376`) never reaches `PTP_LOCKED`, `ptp4l` never emits `CLOCK_CLASS_CHANGE 6`, the phc2sys metric stays at 0, and all three WPC GM assertions fail in turn. Hardware DPLL showing LOCKED (`dpll=1`) is not sufficient per `event_test.go:92–95`.

- **1/14 failures — DualNICBCHA phc2sys failover timeout** (suites: dualnicbcha\[serial\])
  The serial DualNICBCHA phc2sys failover test failed because phc2sys did not switch to the secondary interface within the 60-second test window after the primary was brought down. This may be a timing sensitivity or an infrastructure issue specific to the dualnicbcha topology.

## Actionable Recommendations

1. **Fix `test/pkg/event/event.go` key scheme for `os-clock-sync-state-change` events (resolves 5 failures).** In `createStoredEvent` lines 742–751, use a composite key such as `v.Resource + ":" + string(v.DataType)` so the `"notification"` and `"metric"` entries are distinct even when multiple values share the same ResourceAddress.           if [[ "${USE_UPSTREAM:-false}" == "true" ]]; then
            echo "Running on upstream main branch"
            git clone --single-branch --branch main https://github.com/k8snetworkplumbingwg/ptp-operator.git
          else

          sed -i "s/\(CGO_ENABLED=\${CGO_ENABLED}\) \(GOOS=\${GOOS}\)/\1 CC=\"gcc -fuse-ld=gold\" \2/" hack/build.sh

## Cross-Suite Summary — periodic-ci-openshift-release-main-nightly-5.0-e2e-telco5g-ptp

**Version:** 5.0 | **Total failures:** 36 | **Suites:** bc, dualfollower, dualnicbc, dualnicbcha, oc, tbc, tgm

**TL;DR:** T-GM FREERUN from linuxptp-daemon PR #629 cascades 34 failures; a test key-scheme bug and lab topology gap cause two more.

---

## Root Cause Groups

- **34/36 failures — T-GM ts2phc FREERUN cascading to all downstream suites** (suites: bc, dualfollower, dualnicbc, dualnicbcha, tgm)

  `k8snetworkplumbingwg/linuxptp-daemon` PR #629 (commit `14eb788`, "Sync from upstream 22-Jul-2026", merged 2026-07-22) introduced `addons/intel/e825.go`, whose `setupGnss()` (line 262) fails to locate or enable GNSS pins on node `cnfdf32`, so ts2phc never receives a 1PPS signal and stays in FREERUN (`openshift_ptp_clock_state{process="ts2phc"} 0`) despite the hardware DPLL being LOCKED (`process="dpll"} 1`). With no valid T-GM source, both `ptp4l.0.config` and `ptp4l.1.config` on the downstream BC node `cnfdf30` also stay in FREERUN (clock_class=255, all interfaces in MASTER role, 4 crash/restarts each), phc2sys stays DOWN (status=0), and after `ptphelper.RestartPTPDaemon()` is called in `parallel_suite_test.go:68` the clock cannot re-lock within the parallel event test window, causing every `testSyncState()` retry (30 × 10 s) at `ptp.go:393` to time out across all affected suites.

- **1/36 failures — Event value key-scheme mismatch causes LOCKED state to go undetected** (suite: oc)

  Commit `d20ffcbf` (CNF-19588, 2026-07-03, `main`) changed `test/pkg/event/event.go:742-751` to key `StoredEventValues` by `v.Resource` (the full resource-address path, e.g. `/cluster/node/cnfdf30.../CLOCK_REALTIME`) instead of `string(v.DataType)`, but `test/conformance/parallel/ptp.go:413-415` still reads `values["notification"].(string)` and `values["metric"].(float64)`. Both keys are absent from the new map, so `wasLocked` in `testSyncState()` is never set to `true`, and the test always times out despite the daemon correctly reporting a LOCKED state in the raw CloudEvent payload.

- **1/36 failures — T-BC topology solver finds no valid hardware** (suite: tbc)

  PR #205 (`aede1e93`, merged 2026-06-23, `main`) added T-BC topology tests and the five-constraint solver in `testconfig.go:704-710` (WPC NIC receiver, two same-NIC transmitters, WPC NIC local GM on same LAN). The lab cluster (cnfdf30/31/32) has WPC hardware sufficient for TGM tests but not the multi-port T-BC topology. Rather than calling `Skip()`, `execute.BeforeAll` at `ptp.go:363-368` calls `Fail()` when `CreatePtpConfigurationsWithRetry(3)` returns `"no T-BC solution found for TBC"`, surfacing as a hard failure instead of a lab-capability skip.

---

## Cross-Suite Patterns

| Root Cause | bc | dualfollower | dualnicbc | dualnicbcha | oc | tbc | tgm | Suite-specific? |
|---|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|
| T-GM FREERUN cascade (linuxptp-daemon PR #629) | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | | | ✓ | No — 5 suites |
| Event key-scheme mismatch (commit d20ffcbf) | | | | | ✓ | | | Yes — oc only |
| T-BC topology missing in lab (PR #205) | | | | | | ✓ | | Yes — tbc only |

---

## Actionable Recommendations

1. **Revert or fix linuxptp-daemon PR #629** (`14eb788`): `addons/intel/e825.go`'s `setupGnss()` must handle the case where no matching GNSS netlink pins are found without silently leaving ts2phc unconfigured. Either revert the PR until the GNSS pin discovery is hardened, or add explicit error-path logging and a fallback so that ts2phc FREERUN is surfaced in operator events rather than causing a silent cascade across all 5 downstream suites. This single fix unblocks 34/36 failures.

2. **Fix the event key-scheme reader in `ptp.go:413-415`**: Update `test/conformance/parallel/ptp.go` to iterate the `StoredEventValues` map and match entries by resource-path suffix (`CLOCK_REALTIME`) or by inspecting `data_type` from the raw CloudEvent, consistent with how `event.go:742-751` now stores values after commit `d20ffcbf`. The mismatch is deterministic — `"notification"` and `"metric"` keys no longer exist — so this will always fail until corrected.

3. **Change the T-BC `BeforeAll` hard-fail to a conditional skip**: In `test/conformance/serial/ptp.go:363-368`, replace `Fail(...)` with `Skip(...)` when `CreatePtpConfigurationsWithRetry` returns a topology-not-found error. Additionally, consider gating the T-BC test suite on a feature flag or hardware-capability label so it is not scheduled against clusters that cannot satisfy the solver constraints, preventing spurious failures when no T-BC hardware is available.

**Suite TL;DR:** The single bc-suite failure is `[bc-parallel] Event based tests PTP Slave Clock Sync` erroring after ~364 seconds, because the parallel event infrastructure (consumer → cloud-event-proxy `CurrentState` endpoint) produced no observable `Got CurrentState:` log entries within any of the 30 × 10 s push-attempt windows — consistent with the `"could not push initial event"` code path in `testSyncState`.

    - `parallel_suite_test.go` `SynchronizedBeforeSuite` calls `ptphelper.RestartPTPDaemon()` and `event.CreateConsumerApp(fullConfig.DiscoveredClockUnderTestPod.Spec.NodeName)` before tests run
    - All other parallel event sync tests across every mode also errored simultaneously: `[dualfollower-parallel]`, `[dualnicbc-parallel]`, `[dualnicbcha-parallel]`, `[oc-parallel]` — all `result: error` (from `junit-failures.txt`)
    - BC serial event tests all **passed**: `Running with event enabled Should check for ptp events`, `Should recover clockClass via event API after cloud-event-proxy crash`, `Should receive events after linuxptp-daemon pod restart` — all `result: pass`
    - `test/conformance/parallel/ptp.go` `testSyncState`: `for i = 0; i < 30; i++ { err = event.PushInitialEvent(…, 10*time.Second) }` — 30 × 10 s = 300 s maximum before `Fail("could not push initial event, err=%s", err)`

    - `examples/consumer/main.go:294`: `log.Debugf("Got CurrentState: %s ", string(cloudEvent))` — logged **only** on HTTP 200 from cloud-event-proxy `CurrentState` endpoint; `common.InitLogger()` defaults to `DebugLevel` when `LOG_LEVEL` is unset

    - Neither PR directly changes the event delivery path. **Breaking PR/Commit: Unknown** — most likely a timing/environmental flake triggered by daemon restart recovery time under concurrent multi-mode load.

  - **Is it a flake?** **Yes** — the simultaneous failure of every parallel event sync test across all modes (bc, dualfollower, dualnicbc, dualnicbcha, oc) with passing serial event tests points to a race between `RestartPTPDaemon()` teardown/startup and the consumer app's first 60-second `pullEvents()` window. The `PushInitialEvents` 10 s polling window can miss a 60 s consumer pull cycle if the cloud-event-proxy pod is still initializing. This is a known timing sensitivity in the parallel soak suite setup.

Alternatively, add a readiness gate in `SynchronizedBeforeSuite` that waits until the cloud-event-proxy `CurrentState` endpoint returns HTTP 200 before proceeding.

## Cross-Suite Summary — periodic-ci-openshift-release-main-nightly-5.0-e2e-telco5g-ptp

**Version:** 5.0 | **Total failures:** 36 | **Suites:** bc, dualfollower, dualnicbc, dualnicbcha, oc, tbc, tgm

**TL;DR:** T-GM FREERUN from linuxptp-daemon PR #629 cascades 34 failures; a test key-scheme bug and lab topology gap cause two more.

---

## Root Cause Groups

- **34/36 failures — T-GM ts2phc FREERUN cascading to all downstream suites** (suites: bc, dualfollower, dualnicbc, dualnicbcha, tgm)

  `k8snetworkplumbingwg/linuxptp-daemon` PR #629 (commit `14eb788`, "Sync from upstream 22-Jul-2026", merged 2026-07-22) introduced `addons/intel/e825.go`, whose `setupGnss()` (line 262) fails to locate or enable GNSS pins on node `cnfdf32`, so ts2phc never receives a 1PPS signal and stays in FREERUN (`openshift_ptp_clock_state{process="ts2phc"} 0`) despite the hardware DPLL being LOCKED (`process="dpll"} 1`). With no valid T-GM source, both `ptp4l.0.config` and `ptp4l.1.config` on the downstream BC node `cnfdf30` also stay in FREERUN (clock_class=255, all interfaces in MASTER role, 4 crash/restarts each), phc2sys stays DOWN (status=0), and after `ptphelper.RestartPTPDaemon()` is called in `parallel_suite_test.go:68` the clock cannot re-lock within the parallel event test window, causing every `testSyncState()` retry (30 × 10 s) at `ptp.go:393` to time out across all affected suites.

- **1/36 failures — Event value key-scheme mismatch causes LOCKED state to go undetected** (suite: oc)

  Commit `d20ffcbf` (CNF-19588, 2026-07-03, `main`) changed `test/pkg/event/event.go:742-751` to key `StoredEventValues` by `v.Resource` (the full resource-address path, e.g. `/cluster/node/cnfdf30.../CLOCK_REALTIME`) instead of `string(v.DataType)`, but `test/conformance/parallel/ptp.go:413-415` still reads `values["notification"].(string)` and `values["metric"].(float64)`. Both keys are absent from the new map, so `wasLocked` in `testSyncState()` is never set to `true`, and the test always times out despite the daemon correctly reporting a LOCKED state in the raw CloudEvent payload.

- **1/36 failures — T-BC topology solver finds no valid hardware** (suite: tbc)

  PR #205 (`aede1e93`, merged 2026-06-23, `main`) added T-BC topology tests and the five-constraint solver in `testconfig.go:704-710` (WPC NIC receiver, two same-NIC transmitters, WPC NIC local GM on same LAN). The lab cluster (cnfdf30/31/32) has WPC hardware sufficient for TGM tests but not the multi-port T-BC topology. Rather than calling `Skip()`, `execute.BeforeAll` at `ptp.go:363-368` calls `Fail()` when `CreatePtpConfigurationsWithRetry(3)` returns `"no T-BC solution found for TBC"`, surfacing as a hard failure instead of a lab-capability skip.

## Actionable Recommendations

1. **Revert or fix linuxptp-daemon PR #629** (`14eb788`): `addons/intel/e825.go`'s `setupGnss()` must handle the case where no matching GNSS netlink pins are found without silently leaving ts2phc unconfigured. Either revert the PR until the GNSS pin discovery is hardened, or add explicit error-path logging and a fallback so that ts2phc FREERUN is surfaced in operator events rather than causing a silent cascade across all 5 downstream suites. This single fix unblocks 34/36 failures.

2. **Fix the event key-scheme reader in `ptp.go:413-415`**: Update `test/conformance/parallel/ptp.go` to iterate the `StoredEventValues` map and match entries by resource-path suffix (`CLOCK_REALTIME`) or by inspecting `data_type` from the raw CloudEvent, consistent with how `event.go:742-751` now stores values after commit `d20ffcbf`. The mismatch is deterministic — `"notification"` and `"metric"` keys no longer exist — so this will always fail until corrected.

3. **Change the T-BC `BeforeAll` hard-fail to a conditional skip**: In `test/conformance/serial/ptp.go:363-368`, replace `Fail(...)` with `Skip(...)` when `CreatePtpConfigurationsWithRetry` returns a topology-not-found error. Additionally, consider gating the T-BC test suite on a feature flag or hardware-capability label so it is not scheduled against clusters that cannot satisfy the solver constraints, preventing spurious failures when no T-BC hardware is available.

## Cross-Suite Summary — periodic-ci-openshift-release-main-nightly-5.0-e2e-telco5g-ptp

**Version:** 5.0 | **Total failures:** 36 | **Suites:** bc, dualfollower, dualnicbc, dualnicbcha, oc, tbc, tgm

**TL;DR:** T-GM FREERUN from linuxptp-daemon PR #629 cascades 34 failures; a test key-scheme bug and lab topology gap cause two more.

---

## Root Cause Groups

- **34/36 failures — T-GM ts2phc FREERUN cascading to all downstream suites** (suites: bc, dualfollower, dualnicbc, dualnicbcha, tgm)

  `k8snetworkplumbingwg/linuxptp-daemon` PR #629 (commit `14eb788`, "Sync from upstream 22-Jul-2026", merged 2026-07-22) introduced `addons/intel/e825.go`, whose `setupGnss()` (line 262) fails to locate or enable GNSS pins on node `cnfdf32`, so ts2phc never receives a 1PPS signal and stays in FREERUN (`openshift_ptp_clock_state{process="ts2phc"} 0`) despite the hardware DPLL being LOCKED (`process="dpll"} 1`). With no valid T-GM source, both `ptp4l.0.config` and `ptp4l.1.config` on the downstream BC node `cnfdf30` also stay in FREERUN (clock_class=255, all interfaces in MASTER role, 4 crash/restarts each), phc2sys stays DOWN (status=0), and after `ptphelper.RestartPTPDaemon()` is called in `parallel_suite_test.go:68` the clock cannot re-lock within the parallel event test window, causing every `testSyncState()` retry (30 × 10 s) at `ptp.go:393` to time out across all affected suites.

- **1/36 failures — Event value key-scheme mismatch causes LOCKED state to go undetected** (suite: oc)

  Commit `d20ffcbf` (CNF-19588, 2026-07-03, `main`) changed `test/pkg/event/event.go:742-751` to key `StoredEventValues` by `v.Resource` (the full resource-address path, e.g. `/cluster/node/cnfdf30.../CLOCK_REALTIME`) instead of `string(v.DataType)`, but `test/conformance/parallel/ptp.go:413-415` still reads `values["notification"].(string)` and `values["metric"].(float64)`. Both keys are absent from the new map, so `wasLocked` in `testSyncState()` is never set to `true`, and the test always times out despite the daemon correctly reporting a LOCKED state in the raw CloudEvent payload.

- **1/36 failures — T-BC topology solver finds no valid hardware** (suite: tbc)

  PR #205 (`aede1e93`, merged 2026-06-23, `main`) added T-BC topology tests and the five-constraint solver in `testconfig.go:704-710` (WPC NIC receiver, two same-NIC transmitters, WPC NIC local GM on same LAN). The lab cluster (cnfdf30/31/32) has WPC hardware sufficient for TGM tests but not the multi-port T-BC topology. Rather than calling `Skip()`, `execute.BeforeAll` at `ptp.go:363-368` calls `Fail()` when `CreatePtpConfigurationsWithRetry(3)` returns `"no T-BC solution found for TBC"`, surfacing as a hard failure instead of a lab-capability skip.

## Actionable Recommendations

1. **Revert or fix linuxptp-daemon PR #629** (`14eb788`): `addons/intel/e825.go`'s `setupGnss()` must handle the case where no matching GNSS netlink pins are found without silently leaving ts2phc unconfigured. Either revert the PR until the GNSS pin discovery is hardened, or add explicit error-path logging and a fallback so that ts2phc FREERUN is surfaced in operator events rather than causing a silent cascade across all 5 downstream suites. This single fix unblocks 34/36 failures.

2. **Fix the event key-scheme reader in `ptp.go:413-415`**: Update `test/conformance/parallel/ptp.go` to iterate the `StoredEventValues` map and match entries by resource-path suffix (`CLOCK_REALTIME`) or by inspecting `data_type` from the raw CloudEvent, consistent with how `event.go:742-751` now stores values after commit `d20ffcbf`. The mismatch is deterministic — `"notification"` and `"metric"` keys no longer exist — so this will always fail until corrected.

3. **Change the T-BC `BeforeAll` hard-fail to a conditional skip**: In `test/conformance/serial/ptp.go:363-368`, replace `Fail(...)` with `Skip(...)` when `CreatePtpConfigurationsWithRetry` returns a topology-not-found error. Additionally, consider gating the T-BC test suite on a feature flag or hardware-capability label so it is not scheduled against clusters that cannot satisfy the solver constraints, preventing spurious failures when no T-BC hardware is available.

## Cross-Suite Summary — periodic-ci-openshift-release-main-nightly-5.0-e2e-telco5g-ptp

**Version:** 5.0 | **Total failures:** 36 | **Suites:** bc, dualfollower, dualnicbc, dualnicbcha, oc, tbc, tgm

**TL;DR:** T-GM FREERUN from linuxptp-daemon PR #629 cascades 34 failures; a test key-scheme bug and lab topology gap cause two more.

---

## Root Cause Groups

- **34/36 failures — T-GM ts2phc FREERUN cascading to all downstream suites** (suites: bc, dualfollower, dualnicbc, dualnicbcha, tgm)

  `k8snetworkplumbingwg/linuxptp-daemon` PR #629 (commit `14eb788`, "Sync from upstream 22-Jul-2026", merged 2026-07-22) introduced `addons/intel/e825.go`, whose `setupGnss()` (line 262) fails to locate or enable GNSS pins on node `cnfdf32`, so ts2phc never receives a 1PPS signal and stays in FREERUN (`openshift_ptp_clock_state{process="ts2phc"} 0`) despite the hardware DPLL being LOCKED (`process="dpll"} 1`). With no valid T-GM source, both `ptp4l.0.config` and `ptp4l.1.config` on the downstream BC node `cnfdf30` also stay in FREERUN (clock_class=255, all interfaces in MASTER role, 4 crash/restarts each), phc2sys stays DOWN (status=0), and after `ptphelper.RestartPTPDaemon()` is called in `parallel_suite_test.go:68` the clock cannot re-lock within the parallel event test window, causing every `testSyncState()` retry (30 × 10 s) at `ptp.go:393` to time out across all affected suites.

- **1/36 failures — Event value key-scheme mismatch causes LOCKED state to go undetected** (suite: oc)

  Commit `d20ffcbf` (CNF-19588, 2026-07-03, `main`) changed `test/pkg/event/event.go:742-751` to key `StoredEventValues` by `v.Resource` (the full resource-address path, e.g. `/cluster/node/cnfdf30.../CLOCK_REALTIME`) instead of `string(v.DataType)`, but `test/conformance/parallel/ptp.go:413-415` still reads `values["notification"].(string)` and `values["metric"].(float64)`. Both keys are absent from the new map, so `wasLocked` in `testSyncState()` is never set to `true`, and the test always times out despite the daemon correctly reporting a LOCKED state in the raw CloudEvent payload.

- **1/36 failures — T-BC topology solver finds no valid hardware** (suite: tbc)

  PR #205 (`aede1e93`, merged 2026-06-23, `main`) added T-BC topology tests and the five-constraint solver in `testconfig.go:704-710` (WPC NIC receiver, two same-NIC transmitters, WPC NIC local GM on same LAN). The lab cluster (cnfdf30/31/32) has WPC hardware sufficient for TGM tests but not the multi-port T-BC topology. ## Cross-Suite Summary — periodic-ci-openshift-release-main-nightly-5.0-e2e-telco5g-ptp

**Version:** 5.0 | **Total failures:** 36 | **Suites:** bc, dualfollower, dualnicbc, dualnicbcha, oc, tbc, tgm

**TL;DR:** T-GM FREERUN from linuxptp-daemon PR #629 cascades 34 failures; a test key-scheme bug and lab topology gap cause two more.

---

## Root Cause Groups

- **34/36 failures — T-GM ts2phc FREERUN cascading to all downstream suites** (suites: bc, dualfollower, dualnicbc, dualnicbcha, tgm)

  `k8snetworkplumbingwg/linuxptp-daemon` PR #629 (commit `14eb788`, "Sync from upstream 22-Jul-2026", merged 2026-07-22) introduced `addons/intel/e825.go`, whose `setupGnss()` (line 262) fails to locate or enable GNSS pins on node `cnfdf32`, so ts2phc never receives a 1PPS signal and stays in FREERUN (`openshift_ptp_clock_state{process="ts2phc"} 0`) despite the hardware DPLL being LOCKED (`process="dpll"} 1`). With no valid T-GM source, both `ptp4l.0.config` and `ptp4l.1.config` on the downstream BC node `cnfdf30` also stay in FREERUN (clock_class=255, all interfaces in MASTER role, 4 crash/restarts each), phc2sys stays DOWN (status=0), and after `ptphelper.RestartPTPDaemon()` is called in `parallel_suite_test.go:68` the clock cannot re-lock within the parallel event test window, causing every `testSyncState()` retry (30 × 10 s) at `ptp.go:393` to time out across all affected suites.

- **1/36 failures — Event value key-scheme mismatch causes LOCKED state to go undetected** (suite: oc)

  Commit `d20ffcbf` (CNF-19588, 2026-07-03, `main`) changed `test/pkg/event/event.go:742-751` to key `StoredEventValues` by `v.Resource` (the full resource-address path, e.g. `/cluster/node/cnfdf30.../CLOCK_REALTIME`) instead of `string(v.DataType)`, but `test/conformance/parallel/ptp.go:413-415` still reads `values["notification"].(string)` and `values["metric"].(float64)`. Both keys are absent from the new map, so `wasLocked` in `testSyncState()` is never set to `true`, and the test always times out despite the daemon correctly reporting a LOCKED state in the raw CloudEvent payload.

- **1/36 failures — T-BC topology solver finds no valid hardware** (suite: tbc)

  PR #205 (`aede1e93`, merged 2026-06-23, `main`) added T-BC topology tests and the five-constraint solver in `testconfig.go:704-710` (WPC NIC receiver, two same-NIC transmitters, WPC NIC local GM on same LAN). The lab cluster (cnfdf30/31/32) has WPC hardware sufficient for TGM tests but not the multi-port T-BC topology. Rather than calling `Skip()`, `execute.BeforeAll` at `ptp.go:363-368` calls `Fail()` when `CreatePtpConfigurationsWithRetry(3)` returns `"no T-BC solution found for TBC"`, surfacing as a hard failure instead of a lab-capability skip.

---

| T-BC topology missing in lab (PR #205) | | | | | | ✓ | | Yes — tbc only |

## Actionable Recommendations

1. **Revert or fix linuxptp-daemon PR #629** (`14eb788`): `addons/intel/e825.go`'s `setupGnss()` must handle the case where no matching GNSS netlink pins are found without silently leaving ts2phc unconfigured. Either revert the PR until the GNSS pin discovery is hardened, or add explicit error-path logging and a fallback so that ts2phc FREERUN is surfaced in operator events rather than causing a silent cascade across all 5 downstream suites. This single fix unblocks 34/36 failures.

2. **Fix the event key-scheme reader in `ptp.go:413-415`**: Update `test/conformance/parallel/ptp.go` to iterate the `StoredEventValues` map and match entries by resource-path suffix (`CLOCK_REALTIME`) or by inspecting `data_type` from the raw CloudEvent, consistent with how `event.go:742-751` now stores values after commit `d20ffcbf`. The mismatch is deterministic — `"notification"` and `"metric"` keys no longer exist — so this will always fail until corrected.

3. **Change the T-BC `BeforeAll` hard-fail to a conditional skip**: In `test/conformance/serial/ptp.go:363-368`, replace `Fail(...)` with `Skip(...)` when `CreatePtpConfigurationsWithRetry` returns a topology-not-found error. Additionally, consider gating the T-BC test suite on a feature flag or hardware-capability label so it is not scheduled against clusters that cannot satisfy the solver constraints, preventing spurious failures when no T-BC hardware is available.

## Root Cause Groups

- **34/36 failures — T-GM ts2phc FREERUN cascading to all downstream suites** (suites: bc, dualfollower, dualnicbc, dualnicbcha, tgm)

  `k8snetworkplumbingwg/linuxptp-daemon` PR #629 (commit `14eb788`, "Sync from upstream 22-Jul-2026", merged 2026-07-22) introduced `addons/intel/e825.go`, whose `setupGnss()` (line 262) fails to locate or enable GNSS pins on node `cnfdf32`, so ts2phc never receives a 1PPS signal and stays in FREERUN (`openshift_ptp_clock_state{process="ts2phc"} 0`) despite the hardware DPLL being LOCKED (`process="dpll"} 1`). With no valid T-GM source, both `ptp4l.0.config` and `ptp4l.1.config` on the downstream BC node `cnfdf30` also stay in FREERUN (clock_class=255, all interfaces in MASTER role, 4 crash/restarts each), phc2sys stays DOWN (status=0), and after `ptphelper.RestartPTPDaemon()` is called in `parallel_suite_test.go:68` the clock cannot re-lock within the parallel event test window, causing every `testSyncState()` retry (30 × 10 s) at `ptp.go:393` to time out across all affected suites.

- **1/36 failures — Event value key-scheme mismatch causes LOCKED state to go undetected** (suite: oc)

  Commit `d20ffcbf` (CNF-19588, 2026-07-03, `main`) changed `test/pkg/event/event.go:742-751` to key `StoredEventValues` by `v.Resource` (the full resource-address path, e.g. `/cluster/node/cnfdf30.../CLOCK_REALTIME`) instead of `string(v.DataType)`, but `test/conformance/parallel/ptp.go:413-415` still reads `values["notification"].(string)` and `values["metric"].(float64)`. Both keys are absent from the new map, so `wasLocked` in `testSyncState()` is never set to `true`, and the test always times out despite the daemon correctly reporting a LOCKED state in the raw CloudEvent payload.

- **1/36 failures — T-BC topology solver finds no valid hardware** (suite: tbc)

  PR #205 (`aede1e93`, merged 2026-06-23, `main`) added T-BC topology tests and the five-constraint solver in `testconfig.go:704-710` (WPC NIC receiver, two same-NIC transmitters, WPC NIC local GM on same LAN).
