## Cross-Suite Summary — periodic-ci-openshift-release-main-nightly-5.0-e2e-telco5g-ptp

**Version:** 5.0 | **Total failures:** 36 | **Suites:** bc, dualfollower, dualnicbc, dualnicbcha, oc, tbc, tgm

**TL;DR:** T-GM FREERUN from linuxptp-daemon PR #629 cascades 34 failures; a test key-scheme bug and lab topology gap cause two more.

---

## Root Cause Groups

- **34/36 failures — T-GM ts2phc FREERUN cascading to all downstream suites** (suites: bc, dualfollower, dualnicbc, dualnicbcha, tgm)

  `k8snetworkplumbingwg/linuxptp-daemon` PR #629 (commit `14eb788`, "Sync from upstream 22-Jul-2026", merged 2026-07-22) introduced `addons/intel/e825.go`, whose `setupGnss()` (line 262) fails to locate or enable GNSS pins on node `cnfdf32`, so ts2phc never receives a 1PPS signal and stays in FREERUN (`openshift_ptp_clock_state{process="ts2phc"} 0`) despite the hardware DPLL being LOCKED (`process="dpll"} 1`). With no valid T-GM source, both `ptp4l.0.config` and `ptp4l.1.config` on the downstream BC node `cnfdf30` also stay in FREERUN (clock_class=255, all interfaces in MASTER role, 4 crash/restarts each), phc2sys stays DOWN (status=0), and after `ptphelper.RestartPTPDaemon()` is called in `parallel_suite_test.go:68` the clock cannot re-lock within the parallel event test window, causing every `testSyncState()` retry (30 × 10 s) at `ptp.go:393` to time out across all affected suites.

- **1/36 failures — Event value key-scheme mismatch causes LOCKED state to go undetected** (suite: oc)

  Commit `d20ffcbf` (CNF-19588, 2026-07-03, `main`) changed `test/pkg/event/event.go:742-751` to key `StoredEventValues` by `v.Resource` (the full resource-address path, e.g. `/cluster/node/cnfdf30.../CLOCK_REALTIME`) instead of `string(v.DataType)`, but `test/conformance/parallel/ptp.go:413-415` still reads `values["notification"].(string)` and `values["metric"].(float64)`. Both keys are absent from the new map, so `wasLocked` in `testSyncState()` is never set to `true`, and the test always times out despite the daemon correctly reporting a LOCKED state in the raw CloudEvent payload.

- **1/36 failures — T-BC topology solver finds no valid hardware** (suite: tbc)

  PR #205 (`aede1e93`, merged 2026-06-23, `main`) added T-BC topology tests and the five-constraint solver in `testconfig.go:704-710` (WPC NIC receiver, two same-NIC transmitters, WPC NIC local GM on same LAN). The lab cluster (cnfdf30/31/32) has WPC hardware sufficient for TGM tests but not the multi-port T-BC topology. Rather than calling `Skip()`, `execute.BeforeAll` at `ptp.go:363-368` calls `Fail()` when `CreatePtpConfigurationsWithRetry(3)` returns `"no T-BC solution found for TBC"`, surfacing as a hard failure instead of a lab-capability skip.

## Cross-Suite Summary — periodic-ci-openshift-release-main-nightly-5.0-e2e-telco5g-ptp

**Version:** 5.0 | **Total failures:** 36 | **Suites:** bc, dualfollower, dualnicbc, dualnicbcha, oc, tbc, tgm

**TL;DR:** T-GM FREERUN from linuxptp-daemon PR #629 cascades 34 failures; a test key-scheme bug and lab topology gap cause two more.

---

## Root Cause Groups

- **34/36 failures — T-GM ts2phc FREERUN cascading to all downstream suites** (suites: bc, dualfollower, dualnicbc, dualnicbcha, tgm)

  `k8snetworkplumbingwg/linuxptp-daemon` PR #629 (commit `14eb788`, "Sync from upstream 22-Jul-2026", merged 2026-07-22) introduced `addons/intel/e825.go`, whose `setupGnss()` (line 262) fails to locate or enable GNSS pins on node `cnfdf32`, so ts2phc never receives a 1PPS signal and stays in FREERUN (`openshift_ptp_clock_state{process="ts2phc"} 0`) despite the hardware DPLL being LOCKED (`process="dpll"} 1`). With no valid T-GM source, both `ptp4l.0.config` and `ptp4l.1.config` on the downstream BC node `cnfdf30` also stay in FREERUN (clock_class=255, all interfaces in MASTER role, 4 crash/restarts each), phc2sys stays DOWN (status=0), and after `ptphelper.RestartPTPDaemon()` is called in `parallel_suite_test.go:68` the clock cannot re-lock within the parallel event test window, causing every `testSyncState()` retry (30 × 10 s) at `ptp.go:393` to time out across all affected suites.

- **1/36 failures — Event value key-scheme mismatch causes LOCKED state to go undetected** (suite: oc)

  Commit `d20ffcbf` (CNF-19588, 2026-07-03, `main`) changed `test/pkg/event/event.go:742-751` to key `StoredEventValues` by `v.Resource` (the full resource-address path, e.g. `/cluster/node/cnfdf30.../CLOCK_REALTIME`) instead of `string(v.DataType)`, but `test/conformance/parallel/ptp.go:413-415` still reads `values["notification"].(string)` and `values["metric"].(float64)`. Both keys are absent from the new map, so `wasLocked` in `testSyncState()` is never set to `true`, and the test always times out despite the daemon correctly reporting a LOCKED state in the raw CloudEvent payload.

- **1/36 failures — T-BC topology solver finds no valid hardware** (suite: tbc)

  PR #205 (`aede1e93`, merged 2026-06-23, `main`) added T-BC topology tests and the five-constraint solver in `testconfig.go:704-710` (WPC NIC receiver, two same-NIC transmitters, WPC NIC local GM on same LAN). The lab cluster (cnfdf30/31/32) has WPC hardware sufficient for TGM tests but not the multi-port T-BC topology. Rather than calling `Skip()`, `execute.BeforeAll` at `ptp.go:363-368` calls `Fail()` when `CreatePtpConfigurationsWithRetry(3)` returns `"no T-BC solution found for TBC"`, surfacing as a hard failure instead of a lab-capability skip.

Either revert the PR until the GNSS pin discovery is hardened, or add explicit error-path logging and a fallback so that ts2phc FREERUN is surfaced in operator events rather than causing a silent cascade across all 5 downstream suites. This single fix unblocks 34/36 failures.

2. **Fix the event key-scheme reader in `ptp.go:413-415`**: Update `test/conformance/parallel/ptp.go` to iterate the `StoredEventValues` map and match entries by resource-path suffix (`CLOCK_REALTIME`) or by inspecting `data_type` from the raw CloudEvent, consistent with how `event.go:742-751` now stores values after commit `d20ffcbf`. The mismatch is deterministic — `"notification"` and `"metric"` keys no longer exist — so this will always fail until corrected.

3. **Change the T-BC `BeforeAll` hard-fail to a conditional skip**: In `test/conformance/serial/ptp.go:363-368`, replace `Fail(...)` with `Skip(...)` when `CreatePtpConfigurationsWithRetry` returns a topology-not-found error. ## Cross-Suite Summary — periodic-ci-openshift-release-main-nightly-5.0-e2e-telco5g-ptp

**Version:** 5.0 | **Total failures:** 36 | **Suites:** bc, dualfollower, dualnicbc, dualnicbcha, oc, tbc, tgm

**TL;DR:** T-GM FREERUN from linuxptp-daemon PR #629 cascades 34 failures; a test key-scheme bug and lab topology gap cause two more.

---

## Root Cause Groups

- **34/36 failures — T-GM ts2phc FREERUN cascading to all downstream suites** (suites: bc, dualfollower, dualnicbc, dualnicbcha, tgm)

  `k8snetworkplumbingwg/linuxptp-daemon` PR #629 (commit `14eb788`, "Sync from upstream 22-Jul-2026", merged 2026-07-22) introduced `addons/intel/e825.go`, whose `setupGnss()` (line 262) fails to locate or enable GNSS pins on node `cnfdf32`, so ts2phc never receives a 1PPS signal and stays in FREERUN (`openshift_ptp_clock_state{process="ts2phc"} 0`) despite the hardware DPLL being LOCKED (`process="dpll"} 1`). With no valid T-GM source, both `ptp4l.0.config` and `ptp4l.1.config` on the downstream BC node `cnfdf30` also stay in FREERUN (clock_class=255, all interfaces in MASTER role, 4 crash/restarts each), phc2sys stays DOWN (status=0), and after `ptphelper.RestartPTPDaemon()` is called in `parallel_suite_test.go:68` the clock cannot re-lock within the parallel event test window, causing every `testSyncState()` retry (30 × 10 s) at `ptp.go:393` to time out across all affected suites.

- **1/36 failures — Event value key-scheme mismatch causes LOCKED state to go undetected** (suite: oc)

  Commit `d20ffcbf` (CNF-19588, 2026-07-03, `main`) changed `test/pkg/event/event.go:742-751` to key `StoredEventValues` by `v.Resource` (the full resource-address path, e.g. `/cluster/node/cnfdf30.../CLOCK_REALTIME`) instead of `string(v.DataType)`, but `test/conformance/parallel/ptp.go:413-415` still reads `values["notification"].(string)` and `values["metric"].(float64)`. Both keys are absent from the new map, so `wasLocked` in `testSyncState()` is never set to `true`, and the test always times out despite the daemon correctly reporting a LOCKED state in the raw CloudEvent payload.

- **1/36 failures — T-BC topology solver finds no valid hardware** (suite: tbc)

  PR #205 (`aede1e93`, merged 2026-06-23, `main`) added T-BC topology tests and the five-constraint solver in `testconfig.go:704-710` (WPC NIC receiver, two same-NIC transmitters, WPC NIC local GM on same LAN). The lab cluster (cnfdf30/31/32) has WPC hardware sufficient for TGM tests but not the multi-port T-BC topology. Rather than calling `Skip()`, `execute.BeforeAll` at `ptp.go:363-368` calls `Fail()` when `CreatePtpConfigurationsWithRetry(3)` returns `"no T-BC solution found for TBC"`, surfacing as a hard failure instead of a lab-capability skip.

## Actionable Recommendations

1. **Revert or fix linuxptp-daemon PR #629** (`14eb788`): `addons/intel/e825.go`'s `setupGnss()` must handle the case where no matching GNSS netlink pins are found without silently leaving ts2phc unconfigured. Either revert the PR until the GNSS pin discovery is hardened, or add explicit error-path logging and a fallback so that ts2phc FREERUN is surfaced in operator events rather than causing a silent cascade across all 5 downstream suites. This single fix unblocks 34/36 failures.

2. **Fix the event key-scheme reader in `ptp.go:413-415`**: Update `test/conformance/parallel/ptp.go` to iterate the `StoredEventValues` map and match entries by resource-path suffix (`CLOCK_REALTIME`) or by inspecting `data_type` from the raw CloudEvent, consistent with how `event.go:742-751` now stores values after commit `d20ffcbf`. The mismatch is deterministic — `"notification"` and `"metric"` keys no longer exist — so this will always fail until corrected.

3. **Change the T-BC `BeforeAll` hard-fail to a conditional skip**: In `test/conformance/serial/ptp.go:363-368`, replace `Fail(...)` with `Skip(...)` when `CreatePtpConfigurationsWithRetry` returns a topology-not-found error. Additionally, consider gating the T-BC test suite on a feature flag or hardware-capability label so it is not scheduled against clusters that cannot satisfy the solver constraints, preventing spurious failures when no T-BC hardware is available.

## Root Cause Groups

- **34/36 failures — T-GM ts2phc FREERUN cascading to all downstream suites** (suites: bc, dualfollower, dualnicbc, dualnicbcha, tgm)

  `k8snetworkplumbingwg/linuxptp-daemon` PR #629 (commit `14eb788`, "Sync from upstream 22-Jul-2026", merged 2026-07-22) introduced `addons/intel/e825.go`, whose `setupGnss()` (line 262) fails to locate or enable GNSS pins on node `cnfdf32`, so ts2phc never receives a 1PPS signal and stays in FREERUN (`openshift_ptp_clock_state{process="ts2phc"} 0`) despite the hardware DPLL being LOCKED (`process="dpll"} 1`). With no valid T-GM source, both `ptp4l.0.config` and `ptp4l.1.config` on the downstream BC node `cnfdf30` also stay in FREERUN (clock_class=255, all interfaces in MASTER role, 4 crash/restarts each), phc2sys stays DOWN (status=0), and after `ptphelper.RestartPTPDaemon()` is called in `parallel_suite_test.go:68` the clock cannot re-lock within the parallel event test window, causing every `testSyncState()` retry (30 × 10 s) at `ptp.go:393` to time out across all affected suites.

- **1/36 failures — Event value key-scheme mismatch causes LOCKED state to go undetected** (suite: oc)

  Commit `d20ffcbf` (CNF-19588, 2026-07-03, `main`) changed `test/pkg/event/event.go:742-751` to key `StoredEventValues` by `v.Resource` (the full resource-address path, e.g. `/cluster/node/cnfdf30.../CLOCK_REALTIME`) instead of `string(v.DataType)`, but `test/conformance/parallel/ptp.go:413-415` still reads `values["notification"].(string)` and `values["metric"].(float64)`. ## Cross-Suite Summary — periodic-ci-openshift-release-main-nightly-5.0-e2e-telco5g-ptp

**Version:** 5.0 | **Total failures:** 36 | **Suites:** bc, dualfollower, dualnicbc, dualnicbcha, oc, tbc, tgm

**TL;DR:** T-GM FREERUN from linuxptp-daemon PR #629 cascades 34 failures; a test key-scheme bug and lab topology gap cause two more.

---

## Root Cause Groups

- **34/36 failures — T-GM ts2phc FREERUN cascading to all downstream suites** (suites: bc, dualfollower, dualnicbc, dualnicbcha, tgm)

  `k8snetworkplumbingwg/linuxptp-daemon` PR #629 (commit `14eb788`, "Sync from upstream 22-Jul-2026", merged 2026-07-22) introduced `addons/intel/e825.go`, whose `setupGnss()` (line 262) fails to locate or enable GNSS pins on node `cnfdf32`, so ts2phc never receives a 1PPS signal and stays in FREERUN (`openshift_ptp_clock_state{process="ts2phc"} 0`) despite the hardware DPLL being LOCKED (`process="dpll"} 1`). With no valid T-GM source, both `ptp4l.0.config` and `ptp4l.1.config` on the downstream BC node `cnfdf30` also stay in FREERUN (clock_class=255, all interfaces in MASTER role, 4 crash/restarts each), phc2sys stays DOWN (status=0), and after `ptphelper.RestartPTPDaemon()` is called in `parallel_suite_test.go:68` the clock cannot re-lock within the parallel event test window, causing every `testSyncState()` retry (30 × 10 s) at `ptp.go:393` to time out across all affected suites.

- **1/36 failures — Event value key-scheme mismatch causes LOCKED state to go undetected** (suite: oc)

  Commit `d20ffcbf` (CNF-19588, 2026-07-03, `main`) changed `test/pkg/event/event.go:742-751` to key `StoredEventValues` by `v.Resource` (the full resource-address path, e.g. `/cluster/node/cnfdf30.../CLOCK_REALTIME`) instead of `string(v.DataType)`, but `test/conformance/parallel/ptp.go:413-415` still reads `values["notification"].(string)` and `values["metric"].(float64)`. Both keys are absent from the new map, so `wasLocked` in `testSyncState()` is never set to `true`, and the test always times out despite the daemon correctly reporting a LOCKED state in the raw CloudEvent payload.

- **1/36 failures — T-BC topology solver finds no valid hardware** (suite: tbc)

  PR #205 (`aede1e93`, merged 2026-06-23, `main`) added T-BC topology tests and the five-constraint solver in `testconfig.go:704-710` (WPC NIC receiver, two same-NIC transmitters, WPC NIC local GM on same LAN). The lab cluster (cnfdf30/31/32) has WPC hardware sufficient for TGM tests but not the multi-port T-BC topology. Rather than calling `Skip()`, `execute.BeforeAll` at `ptp.go:363-368` calls `Fail()` when `CreatePtpConfigurationsWithRetry(3)` returns `"no T-BC solution found for TBC"`, surfacing as a hard failure instead of a lab-capability skip.

---

| T-BC topology missing in lab (PR #205) | | | | | | ✓ | | Yes — tbc only |

## Actionable Recommendations

1. **Revert or fix linuxptp-daemon PR #629** (`14eb788`): `addons/intel/e825.go`'s `setupGnss()` must handle the case where no matching GNSS netlink pins are found without silently leaving ts2phc unconfigured. Either revert the PR until the GNSS pin discovery is hardened, or add explicit error-path logging and a fallback so that ts2phc FREERUN is surfaced in operator events rather than causing a silent cascade across all 5 downstream suites. This single fix unblocks 34/36 failures.

2. **Fix the event key-scheme reader in `ptp.go:413-415`**: Update `test/conformance/parallel/ptp.go` to iterate the `StoredEventValues` map and match entries by resource-path suffix (`CLOCK_REALTIME`) or by inspecting `data_type` from the raw CloudEvent, consistent with how `event.go:742-751` now stores values after commit `d20ffcbf`. The mismatch is deterministic — `"notification"` and `"metric"` keys no longer exist — so this will always fail until corrected.

3. **Change the T-BC `BeforeAll` hard-fail to a conditional skip**: In `test/conformance/serial/ptp.go:363-368`, replace `Fail(...)` with `Skip(...)` when `CreatePtpConfigurationsWithRetry` returns a topology-not-found error. Additionally, consider gating the T-BC test suite on a feature flag or hardware-capability label so it is not scheduled against clusters that cannot satisfy the solver constraints, preventing spurious failures when no T-BC hardware is available.

---

## Root Cause Groups

- **34/36 failures — T-GM ts2phc FREERUN cascading to all downstream suites** (suites: bc, dualfollower, dualnicbc, dualnicbcha, tgm)

  `k8snetworkplumbingwg/linuxptp-daemon` PR #629 (commit `14eb788`, "Sync from upstream 22-Jul-2026", merged 2026-07-22) introduced `addons/intel/e825.go`, whose `setupGnss()` (line 262) fails to locate or enable GNSS pins on node `cnfdf32`, so ts2phc never receives a 1PPS signal and stays in FREERUN (`openshift_ptp_clock_state{process="ts2phc"} 0`) despite the hardware DPLL being LOCKED (`process="dpll"} 1`). With no valid T-GM source, both `ptp4l.0.config` and `ptp4l.1.config` on the downstream BC node `cnfdf30` also stay in FREERUN (clock_class=255, all interfaces in MASTER role, 4 crash/restarts each), phc2sys stays DOWN (status=0), and after `ptphelper.RestartPTPDaemon()` is called in `parallel_suite_test.go:68` the clock cannot re-lock within the parallel event test window, causing every `testSyncState()` retry (30 × 10 s) at `ptp.go:393` to time out across all affected suites.

- **1/36 failures — Event value key-scheme mismatch causes LOCKED state to go undetected** (suite: oc)

  Commit `d20ffcbf` (CNF-19588, 2026-07-03, `main`) changed `test/pkg/event/event.go:742-751` to key `StoredEventValues` by `v.Resource` (the full resource-address path, e.g. `/cluster/node/cnfdf30.../CLOCK_REALTIME`) instead of `string(v.DataType)`, but `test/conformance/parallel/ptp.go:413-415` still reads `values["notification"].(string)` and `values["metric"].(float64)`. Both keys are absent from the new map, so `wasLocked` in `testSyncState()` is never set to `true`, and the test always times out despite the daemon correctly reporting a LOCKED state in the raw CloudEvent payload.

- **1/36 failures — T-BC topology solver finds no valid hardware** (suite: tbc)

  PR #205 (`aede1e93`, merged 2026-06-23, `main`) added T-BC topology tests and the five-constraint solver in `testconfig.go:704-710` (WPC NIC receiver, two same-NIC transmitters, WPC NIC local GM on same LAN). The lab cluster (cnfdf30/31/32) has WPC hardware sufficient for TGM tests but not the multi-port T-BC topology. ## Root Cause Groups

- **34/36 failures — T-GM ts2phc FREERUN cascading to all downstream suites** (suites: bc, dualfollower, dualnicbc, dualnicbcha, tgm)

  `k8snetworkplumbingwg/linuxptp-daemon` PR #629 (commit `14eb788`, "Sync from upstream 22-Jul-2026", merged 2026-07-22) introduced `addons/intel/e825.go`, whose `setupGnss()` (line 262) fails to locate or enable GNSS pins on node `cnfdf32`, so ts2phc never receives a 1PPS signal and stays in FREERUN (`openshift_ptp_clock_state{process="ts2phc"} 0`) despite the hardware DPLL being LOCKED (`process="dpll"} 1`). With no valid T-GM source, both `ptp4l.0.config` and `ptp4l.1.config` on the downstream BC node `cnfdf30` also stay in FREERUN (clock_class=255, all interfaces in MASTER role, 4 crash/restarts each), phc2sys stays DOWN (status=0), and after `ptphelper.RestartPTPDaemon()` is called in `parallel_suite_test.go:68` the clock cannot re-lock within the parallel event test window, causing every `testSyncState()` retry (30 × 10 s) at `ptp.go:393` to time out across all affected suites.

  Commit `d20ffcbf` (CNF-19588, 2026-07-03, `main`) changed `test/pkg/event/event.go:742-751` to key `StoredEventValues` by `v.Resource` (the full resource-address path, e.g. `/cluster/node/cnfdf30.../CLOCK_REALTIME`) instead of `string(v.DataType)`, but `test/conformance/parallel/ptp.go:413-415` still reads `values["notification"].(string)` and `values["metric"].(float64)`. Both keys are absent from the new map, so `wasLocked` in `testSyncState()` is never set to `true`, and the test always times out despite the daemon correctly reporting a LOCKED state in the raw CloudEvent payload.

  PR #205 (`aede1e93`, merged 2026-06-23, `main`) added T-BC topology tests and the five-constraint solver in `testconfig.go:704-710` (WPC NIC receiver, two same-NIC transmitters, WPC NIC local GM on same LAN). **Version:** 5.0 | **Total failures:** 36 | **Suites:** bc, dualfollower, dualnicbc, dualnicbcha, oc, tbc, tgm

---

## Root Cause Groups

- **34/36 failures — T-GM ts2phc FREERUN cascading to all downstream suites** (suites: bc, dualfollower, dualnicbc, dualnicbcha, tgm)

  `k8snetworkplumbingwg/linuxptp-daemon` PR #629 (commit `14eb788`, "Sync from upstream 22-Jul-2026", merged 2026-07-22) introduced `addons/intel/e825.go`, whose `setupGnss()` (line 262) fails to locate or enable GNSS pins on node `cnfdf32`, so ts2phc never receives a 1PPS signal and stays in FREERUN (`openshift_ptp_clock_state{process="ts2phc"} 0`) despite the hardware DPLL being LOCKED (`process="dpll"} 1`). With no valid T-GM source, both `ptp4l.0.config` and `ptp4l.1.config` on the downstream BC node `cnfdf30` also stay in FREERUN (clock_class=255, all interfaces in MASTER role, 4 crash/restarts each), phc2sys stays DOWN (status=0), and after `ptphelper.RestartPTPDaemon()` is called in `parallel_suite_test.go:68` the clock cannot re-lock within the parallel event test window, causing every `testSyncState()` retry (30 × 10 s) at `ptp.go:393` to time out across all affected suites.

- **1/36 failures — Event value key-scheme mismatch causes LOCKED state to go undetected** (suite: oc)

  Commit `d20ffcbf` (CNF-19588, 2026-07-03, `main`) changed `test/pkg/event/event.go:742-751` to key `StoredEventValues` by `v.Resource` (the full resource-address path, e.g. `/cluster/node/cnfdf30.../CLOCK_REALTIME`) instead of `string(v.DataType)`, but `test/conformance/parallel/ptp.go:413-415` still reads `values["notification"].(string)` and `values["metric"].(float64)`. Both keys are absent from the new map, so `wasLocked` in `testSyncState()` is never set to `true`, and the test always times out despite the daemon correctly reporting a LOCKED state in the raw CloudEvent payload.

- **1/36 failures — T-BC topology solver finds no valid hardware** (suite: tbc)

  PR #205 (`aede1e93`, merged 2026-06-23, `main`) added T-BC topology tests and the five-constraint solver in `testconfig.go:704-710` (WPC NIC receiver, two same-NIC transmitters, WPC NIC local GM on same LAN). The lab cluster (cnfdf30/31/32) has WPC hardware sufficient for TGM tests but not the multi-port T-BC topology. Rather than calling `Skip()`, `execute.BeforeAll` at `ptp.go:363-368` calls `Fail()` when `CreatePtpConfigurationsWithRetry(3)` returns `"no T-BC solution found for TBC"`, surfacing as a hard failure instead of a lab-capability skip.

### Suite: bc (1 failures)

**Suite TL;DR:** The single bc-suite failure is `[bc-parallel] Event based tests PTP Slave Clock Sync` erroring after ~364 seconds, because the parallel event infrastructure (consumer → cloud-event-proxy `CurrentState` endpoint) produced no observable `Got CurrentState:` log entries within any of the 30 × 10 s push-attempt windows — consistent with the `"could not push initial event"` code path in `testSyncState`.

**Root Cause Groups:**

- **Group 1: PTP event soak test unable to bootstrap initial OsClockSyncStateChange event** (affects: `[It] [bc-parallel] Event based tests PTP Slave Clock Sync`)

  - **Evidence:**
    - `"[It] [bc-parallel] Event based tests PTP Slave Clock Sync": {"time": 363.780672433, "result": "error"}` (from `telco5g-ptp-tests__test_results.json`)
    - Test config logged in suite system-out: `SlaveClockSyncConfig:{TestSpec:{Enable:true FailureThreshold:1 Duration:5}}` (5-minute soak window)
    - `parallel_suite_test.go` `SynchronizedBeforeSuite` calls `ptphelper.RestartPTPDaemon()` and `event.CreateConsumerApp(fullConfig.DiscoveredClockUnderTestPod.Spec.NodeName)` before tests run
    - All other parallel event sync tests across every mode also errored simultaneously: `[dualfollower-parallel]`, `[dualnicbc-parallel]`, `[dualnicbcha-parallel]`, `[oc-parallel]` — all `result: error` (from `junit-failures.txt`)
    - BC serial event tests all **passed**: `Running with event enabled Should check for ptp events`, `Should recover clockClass via event API after cloud-event-proxy crash`, `Should receive events after linuxptp-daemon pod restart` — all `result: pass`
    - `test/conformance/parallel/ptp.go` `testSyncState`: `for i = 0; i < 30; i++ { err = event.PushInitialEvent(…, 10*time.Second) }` — 30 × 10 s = 300 s maximum before `Fail("could not push initial event, err=%s", err)`
    - `PushInitialEvents` (event.go:633) streams consumer pod logs with `TailLines=0` looking for regex `Got CurrentState: ({.*})`
    - `examples/consumer/main.go:294`: `log.Debugf("Got CurrentState: %s ", string(cloudEvent))` — logged **only** on HTTP 200 from cloud-event-proxy `CurrentState` endpoint; `common.InitLogger()` defaults to `DebugLevel` when `LOG_LEVEL` is unset
    - `consumer/main.go:390–399` `pullEvents()` fires 5 s after startup then every `eventPullInterval = 60 s`
    - **Timing arithmetic:** SynchronizedBeforeSuite took 42 s; CPU Utilization test (first test, includes 60 s BeforeAll sleep) ran 430 s; Clock Sync test ran 363 s ≈ 30 × 10 s push retries (300 s) + 63 s overhead/BeforeEach/AfterEach — consistent with **all 30 push attempts timing out**

  - **Root Cause:** After `RestartPTPDaemon()` in `parallel_suite_test.go SynchronizedBeforeSuite`, the cloud-event-proxy sidecar on the BC clock-under-test node (`cnfdf32`) is not yet serving valid responses (HTTP 200) to the consumer app's `getCurrentState` polling. The consumer app therefore never emits `Got CurrentState:` at debug log level, so all 30 × 10 s attempts in `event.PushInitialEvents` (event.go:633) time out, causing `testSyncState` (ptp.go:~393) to abort with `"could not push initial event"`. The cross-cutting simultaneous failure across every parallel mode confirms a node-level or daemon-restart-induced condition rather than a per-mode configuration defect. The serial suite's event tests pass because they run before `RestartPTPDaemon()`.

  - **Breaking PR/Commit:**
    - Both `release-5.0` branches are at HEAD commits merged just before this CI run:
      - `redhat-cne/cloud-event-proxy` release-5.0 = `0a69e4658` — [PR #722 CNF-25885: Widen PTP clock thresholds when NTP failover is enabled](https://github.com/redhat-cne/cloud-event-proxy/pull/722), merged 2026-07-27. Changes only `plugins/ptp_operator/config/config.go` (threshold logic) — **does not touch event delivery or `CurrentState` endpoint**.
      - `openshift/linuxptp-daemon` release-5.0 = `14eb78891` — [PR #629 Sync from upstream (22-Jul-2026)](https://github.com/openshift/linuxptp-daemon/pull/629), merged 2026-07-22. Includes only upstream PR #251 "Cleanup GNR-D Hwconfig documentation and defaults" — documentation/defaults, not event-path code.
    - Backport verified: both commits ARE on their respective `release-5.0` branches (confirmed via GitHub API).
    - Neither PR directly changes the event delivery path. **Breaking PR/Commit: Unknown** — most likely a timing/environmental flake triggered by daemon restart recovery time under concurrent multi-mode load.

  - **Is it a flake?** **Yes** — the simultaneous failure of every parallel event sync test across all modes (bc, dualfollower, dualnicbc, dualnicbcha, oc) with passing serial event tests points to a race between `RestartPTPDaemon()` teardown/startup and the consumer app's first 60-second `pullEvents()` window. The `PushInitialEvents` 10 s polling window can miss a 60 s consumer pull cycle if the cloud-event-proxy pod is still initializing. This is a known timing sensitivity in the parallel soak suite setup.

  - **Suggested Fix:** Retry the CI job to confirm flake status. If it recurs, either increase the `eventPullInterval` or change `PushInitialEvents` to use `TailLines` pointing to all historical logs (`TailLines: nil`) so it catches `Got CurrentState:` entries logged before the stream was opened. Alternatively, add a readiness gate in `SynchronizedBeforeSuite` that waits until the cloud-event-proxy `CurrentState` endpoint returns HTTP 200 before proceeding.

issues.test_name: [It] [bc-parallel] Event based tests PTP Slave Clock Sync
issues.ai_summary:
---

## Cross-Suite Summary — periodic-ci-openshift-release-main-nightly-5.0-e2e-telco5g-ptp-upstream

**Version:** 5.0 | **Total failures:** 36 | **Suites:** bc, dualfollower, dualnicbc, dualnicbcha, tbc, all, tgm

**TL;DR:** Three independent `main`-branch regressions — a test key-scheme bug, a broken PMC invocation, and a T-BC topology mismatch — plus a ts2phc servo regression in the upstream sync caused all 36 failures.

---

## Root Cause Groups

- **2/36 failures — `createStoredEvent()` key-scheme change drops LOCKED state** (suites: bc, dualfollower)
  Commit `d20ffcbf` (PR #171, "CNF-19588") changed `test/pkg/event/event.go`'s `createStoredEvent()` to key the `StoredEventValues` map by `v.Resource` (ResourceAddress) instead of `v.DataType`. For `OsClockSyncState` events both the notification ("LOCKED") and metric ("-18") share the identical ResourceAddress, so the metric silently overwrites the notification in the loop. The test then reads `values["notification"]` and finds nothing, `wasLocked` is never set, and the test times out — even though the production cloud-event-proxy correctly delivered LOCKED.

- **21/36 failures — PMC command split + BC/HA clock stuck at FREERUN (clock class 248)** (suites: dualnicbc, dualnicbcha)
  Commit `14eb788` (PR #629, "Sync from upstream 22-Jul-2026" in `k8snetworkplumbingwg/linuxptp-daemon`) introduced a behavioral regression where pmc receives `GET` and `PARENT_DATA_SET` as two separate argv tokens instead of a single quoted string, returning `bad command: GET` / `bad command: PARENT_DATA_SET` for every PMC call. This prevents the test from reading `parentPortIdentity` or `grandmasterIdentity`, causing role-assertion failures (`ens2f0np0` stays in MASTER instead of SLAVE) and preventing clock class from ever reaching 6. All downstream clock-sync, outage-recovery, event-API, and metrics tests cascade from this single invocation bug.

- **2/36 failures — T-BC topology solver returns zero solutions** (suites: tbc, all)
  Commit `84723c83` (PR #205, "test: Add T-BC CI tests and configuration") added `PtpConfigTelcoBC()` and its `AlgoTelcoBCString="TBC"` constraint set to `test/pkg/testconfig/testconfig.go`, requiring a WPC NIC with receiver + two same-NIC transmitter ports and a co-located WPC GM. The CI cluster (`cnfdf30`–`cnfdf32`) does not have this physical topology — only `cnfdf32` has WPC hardware (confirmed as the TGM node). `SynchronizedBeforeSuite` calls `CreatePtpConfigurationsWithRetry(3)`, the solver returns empty, and the suite is torn down before any test runs.

- **11/36 failures — WPC T-GM ts2phc servo stuck in FREERUN despite DPLL LOCKED** (suite: tgm)
  Also attributable to commit `14eb788` (PR #629 upstream sync). DPLL hardware on `cnfdf32` reports LOCKED (`dpll=1`) confirming valid GNSS/1PPS, but ts2phc software servo stays at FREERUN (`ts2phc=0`), indicating a regression in ts2phc log parsing, servo state-machine advancement, or GM clock-class propagation introduced by the sync (`log_parsing.go:82–153`, `ProcessTs2PhcEvents` in `daemon.go:2134–2190`). With ts2phc in FREERUN, `HandleDelayedPhc2sysStartup` never fires, phc2sys stays down (process_status=0), ptp4l clock class stays at 248, no CloudEvent LOCKED events are emitted, and all log-stream tests hit context deadline.

---

## Cross-Suite Patterns

|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `createStoredEvent()` key-scheme drops LOCKED | ✓ | ✓ | — | — | — | — | — | No (2 suites) |

### Suite: bc (1 failures)

**Suite TL;DR:** The single bc-parallel failure is caused by a test-code regression in `createStoredEvent()` that changed the StoredEventValues map key from `v.DataType` ("notification"/"metric") to `v.Resource` (full ResourceAddress), silently dropping the LOCKED state so the test can never observe it.

**Root Cause Groups:**

- **Group 1: Test code key-scheme change in `createStoredEvent()` silently hides LOCKED state** (affects: `[It] [bc-parallel] Event based tests PTP Slave Clock Sync`)
  - **Evidence:**
    ```
    [ptp.go: 411] got map[eventsource:/sync/sync-status/os-clock-sync-state
      eventtimestamp:2026-07-29 09:44:07.684026654 +0000 UTC
      eventtype:event.sync.sync-status.os-clock-sync-state-change
      eventvalues:map[/cluster/node/cnfdf30.telco5gran.eng.rdu2.redhat.com/CLOCK_REALTIME:-18]]
    [ptp.go: 419] clockOffset=0.000000
    [FAILED] OS Clock was never LOCKED and test timed out
    In [It] at: /tmp/cnf-pDNPW/ptp-operator-conformance-test/test/conformance/parallel/ptp.go:393
    ```
    The raw cloud event data (logged by `event.go: 730`) clearly shows:
    ```json
    {"values":[
      {"ResourceAddress":"...CLOCK_REALTIME","data_type":"notification","value_type":"enumeration","value":"LOCKED"},
      {"ResourceAddress":"...CLOCK_REALTIME","data_type":"metric","value_type":"decimal64.3","value":"-18"}
    ]}
    ```
    The LOCKED event was delivered, but `values["notification"]` and `values["metric"]` were both `nil` in the test.

  - **Root Cause:** Commit `d20ffcbf` (PR #171, `CNF-19588`) changed `createStoredEvent()` in `test/pkg/event/event.go` (v1 path lines 711–717, v2 path lines 742–751) from using `v.DataType` as the map key to using `v.Resource` (the ResourceAddress). For `OsClockSyncState` events the notification value and metric value **share the same ResourceAddress** (`/cluster/node/.../CLOCK_REALTIME`), so the metric entry (`-18`) overwrites the notification entry (`LOCKED`) in the loop. The test at `ptp.go:414-415` then reads `values["notification"]` and `values["metric"]` — both return nil because those keys no longer exist — so `state` is `""` instead of `"LOCKED"`, `wasLocked` is never set `true`, and the test times out at `ptp.go:393`.

  - **Breaking PR/Commit:** Commit `d20ffcbf0cecd1cf94987788c703fa8d4565ba4d` — "CNF-19588: CI test for clockClass recovery after cloud-event-proxy crash" (merged as [PR #171](https://github.com/k8snetworkplumbingwg/ptp-operator/pull/171) on `main`). This is a `main`-only test code change; the `release-5.0` production images are unaffected. The OS clock on the hardware IS reaching LOCKED — the cloud event confirms it — but the test framework can't see it.

  - **Is it a flake?** No — the bug is deterministic. Every run will fail to observe LOCKED until the test times out.

  - **Suggested Fix:** In `test/pkg/event/event.go`'s `createStoredEvent()`, use a composite key `<ResourceAddress>:<DataType>` (or fall back to `DataType` when ResourceAddress is empty), so that OsClockSyncState events retain distinct "notification" and "metric" entries while BC clock class events with multiple "metric" values on different resources still don't collide. Alternatively, update `ptp.go:414-415` to iterate the values map and match by DataType rather than by fixed string keys.

**Suite Issue Class:** test_regression
**Suite Severity:** HIGH

  - **Root Cause:** Commit `d20ffcbf` ("CNF-19588: CI test for clockClass recovery after cloud-event-proxy crash", 2026-07-03) changed `createStoredEvent()` in `test/pkg/event/event.go` to use `v.Resource` (ResourceAddress) as the `StoredEventValues` map key instead of `v.DataType`. ## Root Cause Groups

- **2/36 failures — `createStoredEvent()` key-scheme change drops LOCKED state** (suites: bc, dualfollower)
  Commit `d20ffcbf` (PR #171, "CNF-19588") changed `test/pkg/event/event.go`'s `createStoredEvent()` to key the `StoredEventValues` map by `v.Resource` (ResourceAddress) instead of `v.DataType`. - **21/36 failures — PMC command split + BC/HA clock stuck at FREERUN (clock class 248)** (suites: dualnicbc, dualnicbcha)
  Commit `14eb788` (PR #629, "Sync from upstream 22-Jul-2026" in `k8snetworkplumbingwg/linuxptp-daemon`) introduced a behavioral regression where pmc receives `GET` and `PARENT_DATA_SET` as two separate argv tokens instead of a single quoted string, returning `bad command: GET` / `bad command: PARENT_DATA_SET` for every PMC call. ### Suite: bc (1 failures)

**Suite TL;DR:** The single bc-parallel failure is caused by a test-code regression in `createStoredEvent()` that changed the StoredEventValues map key from `v.DataType` ("notification"/"metric") to `v.Resource` (full ResourceAddress), silently dropping the LOCKED state so the test can never observe it.

**Root Cause Groups:**

- **Group 1: Test code key-scheme change in `createStoredEvent()` silently hides LOCKED state** (affects: `[It] [bc-parallel] Event based tests PTP Slave Clock Sync`)
  - **Evidence:**
    ```
    [ptp.go: 411] got map[eventsource:/sync/sync-status/os-clock-sync-state
      eventtimestamp:2026-07-29 09:44:07.684026654 +0000 UTC
      eventtype:event.sync.sync-status.os-clock-sync-state-change
      eventvalues:map[/cluster/node/cnfdf30.telco5gran.eng.rdu2.redhat.com/CLOCK_REALTIME:-18]]
    [ptp.go: 419] clockOffset=0.000000
    [FAILED] OS Clock was never LOCKED and test timed out
    In [It] at: /tmp/cnf-pDNPW/ptp-operator-conformance-test/test/conformance/parallel/ptp.go:393
    ```
    The raw cloud event data (logged by `event.go: 730`) clearly shows:
    ```json
    {"values":[
      {"ResourceAddress":"...CLOCK_REALTIME","data_type":"notification","value_type":"enumeration","value":"LOCKED"},
      {"ResourceAddress":"...CLOCK_REALTIME","data_type":"metric","value_type":"decimal64.3","value":"-18"}
    ]}
    ```
    The LOCKED event was delivered, but `values["notification"]` and `values["metric"]` were both `nil` in the test.

  - **Root Cause:** Commit `d20ffcbf` (PR #171, `CNF-19588`) changed `createStoredEvent()` in `test/pkg/event/event.go` (v1 path lines 711–717, v2 path lines 742–751) from using `v.DataType` as the map key to using `v.Resource` (the ResourceAddress). For `OsClockSyncState` events the notification value and metric value **share the same ResourceAddress** (`/cluster/node/.../CLOCK_REALTIME`), so the metric entry (`-18`) overwrites the notification entry (`LOCKED`) in the loop. The test at `ptp.go:414-415` then reads `values["notification"]` and `values["metric"]` — both return nil because those keys no longer exist — so `state` is `""` instead of `"LOCKED"`, `wasLocked` is never set `true`, and the test times out at `ptp.go:393`.

  - **Breaking PR/Commit:** Commit `d20ffcbf0cecd1cf94987788c703fa8d4565ba4d` — "CNF-19588: CI test for clockClass recovery after cloud-event-proxy crash" (merged as [PR #171](https://github.com/k8snetworkplumbingwg/ptp-operator/pull/171) on `main`). This is a `main`-only test code change; the `release-5.0` production images are unaffected. The OS clock on the hardware IS reaching LOCKED — the cloud event confirms it — but the test framework can't see it.

  - **Is it a flake?** No — the bug is deterministic. Every run will fail to observe LOCKED until the test times out.

  - **Suggested Fix:** In `test/pkg/event/event.go`'s `createStoredEvent()`, use a composite key `<ResourceAddress>:<DataType>` (or fall back to `DataType` when ResourceAddress is empty), so that OsClockSyncState events retain distinct "notification" and "metric" entries while BC clock class events with multiple "metric" values on different resources still don't collide. Alternatively, update `ptp.go:414-415` to iterate the values map and match by DataType rather than by fixed string keys.

**Suite Issue Class:** test_regression
**Suite Severity:** HIGH

  - **Root Cause:** Commit `d20ffcbf` ("CNF-19588: CI test for clockClass recovery after cloud-event-proxy crash", 2026-07-03) changed `createStoredEvent()` in `test/pkg/event/event.go` to use `v.Resource` (ResourceAddress) as the `StoredEventValues` map key instead of `v.DataType`. ## Cross-Suite Summary — periodic-ci-openshift-release-main-nightly-5.0-e2e-telco5g-ptp-upstream

**Version:** 5.0 | **Total failures:** 36 | **Suites:** bc, dualfollower, dualnicbc, dualnicbcha, tbc, all, tgm

**TL;DR:** Three independent `main`-branch regressions — a test key-scheme bug, a broken PMC invocation, and a T-BC topology mismatch — plus a ts2phc servo regression in the upstream sync caused all 36 failures.

---

## Root Cause Groups

- **2/36 failures — `createStoredEvent()` key-scheme change drops LOCKED state** (suites: bc, dualfollower)
  Commit `d20ffcbf` (PR #171, "CNF-19588") changed `test/pkg/event/event.go`'s `createStoredEvent()` to key the `StoredEventValues` map by `v.Resource` (ResourceAddress) instead of `v.DataType`. For `OsClockSyncState` events both the notification ("LOCKED") and metric ("-18") share the identical ResourceAddress, so the metric silently overwrites the notification in the loop. The test then reads `values["notification"]` and finds nothing, `wasLocked` is never set, and the test times out — even though the production cloud-event-proxy correctly delivered LOCKED.

- **21/36 failures — PMC command split + BC/HA clock stuck at FREERUN (clock class 248)** (suites: dualnicbc, dualnicbcha)
  Commit `14eb788` (PR #629, "Sync from upstream 22-Jul-2026" in `k8snetworkplumbingwg/linuxptp-daemon`) introduced a behavioral regression where pmc receives `GET` and `PARENT_DATA_SET` as two separate argv tokens instead of a single quoted string, returning `bad command: GET` / `bad command: PARENT_DATA_SET` for every PMC call. This prevents the test from reading `parentPortIdentity` or `grandmasterIdentity`, causing role-assertion failures (`ens2f0np0` stays in MASTER instead of SLAVE) and preventing clock class from ever reaching 6. All downstream clock-sync, outage-recovery, event-API, and metrics tests cascade from this single invocation bug.

- **2/36 failures — T-BC topology solver returns zero solutions** (suites: tbc, all)
  Commit `84723c83` (PR #205, "test: Add T-BC CI tests and configuration") added `PtpConfigTelcoBC()` and its `AlgoTelcoBCString="TBC"` constraint set to `test/pkg/testconfig/testconfig.go`, requiring a WPC NIC with receiver + two same-NIC transmitter ports and a co-located WPC GM. The CI cluster (`cnfdf30`–`cnfdf32`) does not have this physical topology — only `cnfdf32` has WPC hardware (confirmed as the TGM node). `SynchronizedBeforeSuite` calls `CreatePtpConfigurationsWithRetry(3)`, the solver returns empty, and the suite is torn down before any test runs.

- **11/36 failures — WPC T-GM ts2phc servo stuck in FREERUN despite DPLL LOCKED** (suite: tgm)
  Also attributable to commit `14eb788` (PR #629 upstream sync). DPLL hardware on `cnfdf32` reports LOCKED (`dpll=1`) confirming valid GNSS/1PPS, but ts2phc software servo stays at FREERUN (`ts2phc=0`), indicating a regression in ts2phc log parsing, servo state-machine advancement, or GM clock-class propagation introduced by the sync (`log_parsing.go:82–153`, `ProcessTs2PhcEvents` in `daemon.go:2134–2190`). With ts2phc in FREERUN, `HandleDelayedPhc2sysStartup` never fires, phc2sys stays down (process_status=0), ptp4l clock class stays at 248, no CloudEvent LOCKED events are emitted, and all log-stream tests hit context deadline.

## Actionable Recommendations

1. **Revert or fix `14eb788` (PR #629 upstream sync) in `k8snetworkplumbingwg/linuxptp-daemon`** — This single commit accounts for 32/36 failures across dualnicbc, dualnicbcha, and tgm. Fix the PMC invocation so `GET PARENT_DATA_SET` is passed as a single argv token (not split), and investigate the ts2phc servo state-machine regression to restore LOCKED propagation from DPLL to ts2phc. Until fixed, block this image from nightly jobs or pin to the pre-`14eb788` image.

2. **Fix `createStoredEvent()` key collision in `test/pkg/event/event.go`** (commit `d20ffcbf`, PR #171) — Change the `StoredEventValues` map key from `v.Resource` alone to a composite `<ResourceAddress>:<DataType>` (or revert to `v.DataType`). This eliminates the 2 bc/dualfollower failures immediately with a one-line change. Add a unit test asserting that a `CLOCK_REALTIME` event with both a notification and a metric entry produces two distinct map entries.

3. **Add a `Skip()` guard in the T-BC suite setup** (commit `84723c83`, PR #205) — In `PtpConfigTelcoBC()` or the T-BC `SynchronizedBeforeSuite`, replace the hard `Expect(err).To(BeNil())` with a `Skip()` when the topology solver returns no solution. This prevents 2 suite-level failures and unblocks CI reporting for the rest of the job. Separately, work with the lab team to provision a WPC node satisfying the T-BC constraint (receiver + ≥2 same-NIC transmitters + co-located WPC GM) so the test can eventually run end-to-end.

## Cross-Suite Summary — periodic-ci-openshift-release-main-nightly-5.0-e2e-telco5g-ptp-upstream

**Version:** 5.0 | **Total failures:** 36 | **Suites:** bc, dualfollower, dualnicbc, dualnicbcha, tbc, all, tgm

**TL;DR:** Three independent `main`-branch regressions — a test key-scheme bug, a broken PMC invocation, and a T-BC topology mismatch — plus a ts2phc servo regression in the upstream sync caused all 36 failures.

---

## Root Cause Groups

- **2/36 failures — `createStoredEvent()` key-scheme change drops LOCKED state** (suites: bc, dualfollower)
  Commit `d20ffcbf` (PR #171, "CNF-19588") changed `test/pkg/event/event.go`'s `createStoredEvent()` to key the `StoredEventValues` map by `v.Resource` (ResourceAddress) instead of `v.DataType`. For `OsClockSyncState` events both the notification ("LOCKED") and metric ("-18") share the identical ResourceAddress, so the metric silently overwrites the notification in the loop. The test then reads `values["notification"]` and finds nothing, `wasLocked` is never set, and the test times out — even though the production cloud-event-proxy correctly delivered LOCKED.

- **21/36 failures — PMC command split + BC/HA clock stuck at FREERUN (clock class 248)** (suites: dualnicbc, dualnicbcha)
  Commit `14eb788` (PR #629, "Sync from upstream 22-Jul-2026" in `k8snetworkplumbingwg/linuxptp-daemon`) introduced a behavioral regression where pmc receives `GET` and `PARENT_DATA_SET` as two separate argv tokens instead of a single quoted string, returning `bad command: GET` / `bad command: PARENT_DATA_SET` for every PMC call. This prevents the test from reading `parentPortIdentity` or `grandmasterIdentity`, causing role-assertion failures (`ens2f0np0` stays in MASTER instead of SLAVE) and preventing clock class from ever reaching 6. All downstream clock-sync, outage-recovery, event-API, and metrics tests cascade from this single invocation bug.

- **2/36 failures — T-BC topology solver returns zero solutions** (suites: tbc, all)
  Commit `84723c83` (PR #205, "test: Add T-BC CI tests and configuration") added `PtpConfigTelcoBC()` and its `AlgoTelcoBCString="TBC"` constraint set to `test/pkg/testconfig/testconfig.go`, requiring a WPC NIC with receiver + two same-NIC transmitter ports and a co-located WPC GM. The CI cluster (`cnfdf30`–`cnfdf32`) does not have this physical topology — only `cnfdf32` has WPC hardware (confirmed as the TGM node). `SynchronizedBeforeSuite` calls `CreatePtpConfigurationsWithRetry(3)`, the solver returns empty, and the suite is torn down before any test runs.

- **11/36 failures — WPC T-GM ts2phc servo stuck in FREERUN despite DPLL LOCKED** (suite: tgm)
  Also attributable to commit `14eb788` (PR #629 upstream sync). DPLL hardware on `cnfdf32` reports LOCKED (`dpll=1`) confirming valid GNSS/1PPS, but ts2phc software servo stays at FREERUN (`ts2phc=0`), indicating a regression in ts2phc log parsing, servo state-machine advancement, or GM clock-class propagation introduced by the sync (`log_parsing.go:82–153`, `ProcessTs2PhcEvents` in `daemon.go:2134–2190`). ### Suite: bc (1 failures)

**Suite TL;DR:** The single bc-parallel failure is caused by a test-code regression in `createStoredEvent()` that changed the StoredEventValues map key from `v.DataType` ("notification"/"metric") to `v.Resource` (full ResourceAddress), silently dropping the LOCKED state so the test can never observe it.

**Root Cause Groups:**

- **Group 1: Test code key-scheme change in `createStoredEvent()` silently hides LOCKED state** (affects: `[It] [bc-parallel] Event based tests PTP Slave Clock Sync`)
  - **Evidence:**
    ```
    [ptp.go: 411] got map[eventsource:/sync/sync-status/os-clock-sync-state
      eventtimestamp:2026-07-29 09:44:07.684026654 +0000 UTC
      eventtype:event.sync.sync-status.os-clock-sync-state-change
      eventvalues:map[/cluster/node/cnfdf30.telco5gran.eng.rdu2.redhat.com/CLOCK_REALTIME:-18]]
    [ptp.go: 419] clockOffset=0.000000
    [FAILED] OS Clock was never LOCKED and test timed out
    In [It] at: /tmp/cnf-pDNPW/ptp-operator-conformance-test/test/conformance/parallel/ptp.go:393
    ```
    The raw cloud event data (logged by `event.go: 730`) clearly shows:
    ```json
    {"values":[
      {"ResourceAddress":"...CLOCK_REALTIME","data_type":"notification","value_type":"enumeration","value":"LOCKED"},
      {"ResourceAddress":"...CLOCK_REALTIME","data_type":"metric","value_type":"decimal64.3","value":"-18"}
    ]}
    ```
    The LOCKED event was delivered, but `values["notification"]` and `values["metric"]` were both `nil` in the test.

  - **Root Cause:** Commit `d20ffcbf` (PR #171, `CNF-19588`) changed `createStoredEvent()` in `test/pkg/event/event.go` (v1 path lines 711–717, v2 path lines 742–751) from using `v.DataType` as the map key to using `v.Resource` (the ResourceAddress). For `OsClockSyncState` events the notification value and metric value **share the same ResourceAddress** (`/cluster/node/.../CLOCK_REALTIME`), so the metric entry (`-18`) overwrites the notification entry (`LOCKED`) in the loop. The test at `ptp.go:414-415` then reads `values["notification"]` and `values["metric"]` — both return nil because those keys no longer exist — so `state` is `""` instead of `"LOCKED"`, `wasLocked` is never set `true`, and the test times out at `ptp.go:393`.

  - **Breaking PR/Commit:** Commit `d20ffcbf0cecd1cf94987788c703fa8d4565ba4d` — "CNF-19588: CI test for clockClass recovery after cloud-event-proxy crash" (merged as [PR #171](https://github.com/k8snetworkplumbingwg/ptp-operator/pull/171) on `main`). This is a `main`-only test code change; the `release-5.0` production images are unaffected. The OS clock on the hardware IS reaching LOCKED — the cloud event confirms it — but the test framework can't see it.

  - **Is it a flake?** No — the bug is deterministic. Every run will fail to observe LOCKED until the test times out.

  - **Suggested Fix:** In `test/pkg/event/event.go`'s `createStoredEvent()`, use a composite key `<ResourceAddress>:<DataType>` (or fall back to `DataType` when ResourceAddress is empty), so that OsClockSyncState events retain distinct "notification" and "metric" entries while BC clock class events with multiple "metric" values on different resources still don't collide. Alternatively, update `ptp.go:414-415` to iterate the values map and match by DataType rather than by fixed string keys.

**Suite Issue Class:** test_regression
**Suite Severity:** HIGH

**Suite TL;DR:** The single dualfollower failure is a deterministic test regression introduced in `main`'s test parsing code — events ARE delivered by the production image but the test script can no longer extract the LOCKED state from them, causing an inevitable timeout.

**Root Cause Groups:**

    ```

        type: event.sync.sync-status.os-clock-sync-state-change
      Data,
        {"version":"1.0","values":[
          {"ResourceAddress":"/cluster/node/cnfdf30.../CLOCK_REALTIME","data_type":"notification","value_type":"enumeration","value":"LOCKED"},
          {"ResourceAddress":"/cluster/node/cnfdf30.../CLOCK_REALTIME","data_type":"metric","value_type":"decimal64.3","value":"-18"}
        ]}

    DEBUG [Jul 29 09:44:44.700][ptp.go: 411] got map[eventsource:/sync/sync-status/os-clock-sync-state
      eventvalues:map[/cluster/node/cnfdf30.telco5gran.eng.rdu2.redhat.com/CLOCK_REALTIME:-18]]

    DEBUG [Jul 29 09:44:44.700][ptp.go: 419] clockOffset=0.000000

    [FAILED] OS Clock was never LOCKED and test timed out
    In [It] at: /tmp/cnf-pDNPW/ptp-operator-conformance-test/test/conformance/parallel/ptp.go:393
    ```
  - **Root Cause:** Commit `d20ffcbf` ("CNF-19588: CI test for clockClass recovery after cloud-event-proxy crash", 2026-07-03) changed `createStoredEvent()` in `test/pkg/event/event.go` to use `v.Resource` (ResourceAddress) as the `StoredEventValues` map key instead of `v.DataType`. For `OsClockSyncStateChange` events, both the notification entry ("LOCKED") and the metric entry ("-18") carry the **identical** ResourceAddress (`/cluster/node/.../CLOCK_REALTIME`), so the metric value silently overwrites the notification value, leaving a one-entry map keyed by the path. The test at `ptp.go:414` then does `values["notification"].(string)`, which finds nothing (key is now a full resource path, not "notification"), so `state` is always `""`, `wasLocked` is never set to `true`, and the test times out at `ptp.go:393`. The cloud-event-proxy production image (`release-5.0`) is delivering the LOCKED event correctly — the bug is entirely in the test-framework parsing code on `main`. Because the job pulls test scripts from `main` (`TEST_BRANCH=main`), this commit is the direct root cause.
  - **Breaking PR/Commit:** `d20ffcbf` — "CNF-19588: CI test for clockClass recovery after cloud-event-proxy crash" (2026-07-03, author jackding@gmail.com) — see https://github.com/openshift/ptp-operator/commit/d20ffcbf0cecd1cf94987788c703fa8d4565ba4d
  - **Is it a flake?** No — this is deterministic; every run with this test code and this event shape will produce the same timeout.
  - **Suggested Fix:** In `createStoredEvent()` (`test/pkg/event/event.go` lines ~711–718 for v1, ~742–752 for v2), when the ResourceAddress is non-empty, store values under **both** the resource path key AND the `DataType` key (or always use `DataType` as the primary key and resource path as a secondary key for BC multi-metric disambiguation). Alternatively, update the consumer in `ptp.go:413–415` to iterate over `values` looking for a string value equal to `"LOCKED"` or `"FREERUN"` rather than hardcoding `values["notification"]`.

## Cross-Suite Summary — periodic-ci-openshift-release-main-nightly-5.0-e2e-telco5g-ptp-upstream

**Version:** 5.0 | **Total failures:** 36 | **Suites:** bc, dualfollower, dualnicbc, dualnicbcha, tbc, all, tgm

**TL;DR:** Three independent `main`-branch regressions — a test key-scheme bug, a broken PMC invocation, and a T-BC topology mismatch — plus a ts2phc servo regression in the upstream sync caused all 36 failures.

---

## Root Cause Groups

- **2/36 failures — `createStoredEvent()` key-scheme change drops LOCKED state** (suites: bc, dualfollower)
  Commit `d20ffcbf` (PR #171, "CNF-19588") changed `test/pkg/event/event.go`'s `createStoredEvent()` to key the `StoredEventValues` map by `v.Resource` (ResourceAddress) instead of `v.DataType`. For `OsClockSyncState` events both the notification ("LOCKED") and metric ("-18") share the identical ResourceAddress, so the metric silently overwrites the notification in the loop. The test then reads `values["notification"]` and finds nothing, `wasLocked` is never set, and the test times out — even though the production cloud-event-proxy correctly delivered LOCKED.

- **21/36 failures — PMC command split + BC/HA clock stuck at FREERUN (clock class 248)** (suites: dualnicbc, dualnicbcha)
  Commit `14eb788` (PR #629, "Sync from upstream 22-Jul-2026" in `k8snetworkplumbingwg/linuxptp-daemon`) introduced a behavioral regression where pmc receives `GET` and `PARENT_DATA_SET` as two separate argv tokens instead of a single quoted string, returning `bad command: GET` / `bad command: PARENT_DATA_SET` for every PMC call. This prevents the test from reading `parentPortIdentity` or `grandmasterIdentity`, causing role-assertion failures (`ens2f0np0` stays in MASTER instead of SLAVE) and preventing clock class from ever reaching 6. All downstream clock-sync, outage-recovery, event-API, and metrics tests cascade from this single invocation bug.

- **2/36 failures — T-BC topology solver returns zero solutions** (suites: tbc, all)
  Commit `84723c83` (PR #205, "test: Add T-BC CI tests and configuration") added `PtpConfigTelcoBC()` and its `AlgoTelcoBCString="TBC"` constraint set to `test/pkg/testconfig/testconfig.go`, requiring a WPC NIC with receiver + two same-NIC transmitter ports and a co-located WPC GM. The CI cluster (`cnfdf30`–`cnfdf32`) does not have this physical topology — only `cnfdf32` has WPC hardware (confirmed as the TGM node). `SynchronizedBeforeSuite` calls `CreatePtpConfigurationsWithRetry(3)`, the solver returns empty, and the suite is torn down before any test runs.

- **11/36 failures — WPC T-GM ts2phc servo stuck in FREERUN despite DPLL LOCKED** (suite: tgm)
  Also attributable to commit `14eb788` (PR #629 upstream sync). DPLL hardware on `cnfdf32` reports LOCKED (`dpll=1`) confirming valid GNSS/1PPS, but ts2phc software servo stays at FREERUN (`ts2phc=0`), indicating a regression in ts2phc log parsing, servo state-machine advancement, or GM clock-class propagation introduced by the sync (`log_parsing.go:82–153`, `ProcessTs2PhcEvents` in `daemon.go:2134–2190`). With ts2phc in FREERUN, `HandleDelayedPhc2sysStartup` never fires, phc2sys stays down (process_status=0), ptp4l clock class stays at 248, no CloudEvent LOCKED events are emitted, and all log-stream tests hit context deadline.

### Suite: bc (1 failures)

**Suite TL;DR:** The single bc-parallel failure is caused by a test-code regression in `createStoredEvent()` that changed the StoredEventValues map key from `v.DataType` ("notification"/"metric") to `v.Resource` (full ResourceAddress), silently dropping the LOCKED state so the test can never observe it.

**Root Cause Groups:**

- **Group 1: Test code key-scheme change in `createStoredEvent()` silently hides LOCKED state** (affects: `[It] [bc-parallel] Event based tests PTP Slave Clock Sync`)
  - **Evidence:**
    ```
    [ptp.go: 411] got map[eventsource:/sync/sync-status/os-clock-sync-state
      eventtimestamp:2026-07-29 09:44:07.684026654 +0000 UTC
      eventtype:event.sync.sync-status.os-clock-sync-state-change
      eventvalues:map[/cluster/node/cnfdf30.telco5gran.eng.rdu2.redhat.com/CLOCK_REALTIME:-18]]
    [ptp.go: 419] clockOffset=0.000000
    [FAILED] OS Clock was never LOCKED and test timed out
    In [It] at: /tmp/cnf-pDNPW/ptp-operator-conformance-test/test/conformance/parallel/ptp.go:393
    ```
    The raw cloud event data (logged by `event.go: 730`) clearly shows:
    ```json
    {"values":[
      {"ResourceAddress":"...CLOCK_REALTIME","data_type":"notification","value_type":"enumeration","value":"LOCKED"},
      {"ResourceAddress":"...CLOCK_REALTIME","data_type":"metric","value_type":"decimal64.3","value":"-18"}
    ]}
    ```
    The LOCKED event was delivered, but `values["notification"]` and `values["metric"]` were both `nil` in the test.

  - **Root Cause:** Commit `d20ffcbf` (PR #171, `CNF-19588`) changed `createStoredEvent()` in `test/pkg/event/event.go` (v1 path lines 711–717, v2 path lines 742–751) from using `v.DataType` as the map key to using `v.Resource` (the ResourceAddress). For `OsClockSyncState` events the notification value and metric value **share the same ResourceAddress** (`/cluster/node/.../CLOCK_REALTIME`), so the metric entry (`-18`) overwrites the notification entry (`LOCKED`) in the loop. The test at `ptp.go:414-415` then reads `values["notification"]` and `values["metric"]` — both return nil because those keys no longer exist — so `state` is `""` instead of `"LOCKED"`, `wasLocked` is never set `true`, and the test times out at `ptp.go:393`.

  - **Breaking PR/Commit:** Commit `d20ffcbf0cecd1cf94987788c703fa8d4565ba4d` — "CNF-19588: CI test for clockClass recovery after cloud-event-proxy crash" (merged as [PR #171](https://github.com/k8snetworkplumbingwg/ptp-operator/pull/171) on `main`). This is a `main`-only test code change; the `release-5.0` production images are unaffected. The OS clock on the hardware IS reaching LOCKED — the cloud event confirms it — but the test framework can't see it.

  - **Is it a flake?** No — the bug is deterministic. Every run will fail to observe LOCKED until the test times out.

  - **Suggested Fix:** In `test/pkg/event/event.go`'s `createStoredEvent()`, use a composite key `<ResourceAddress>:<DataType>` (or fall back to `DataType` when ResourceAddress is empty), so that OsClockSyncState events retain distinct "notification" and "metric" entries while BC clock class events with multiple "metric" values on different resources still don't collide. Alternatively, update `ptp.go:414-415` to iterate the values map and match by DataType rather than by fixed string keys.

**Suite Issue Class:** test_regression
**Suite Severity:** HIGH

## Cross-Suite Summary — periodic-ci-openshift-release-main-nightly-5.0-e2e-telco5g-ptp-upstream

**Version:** 5.0 | **Total failures:** 36 | **Suites:** bc, dualfollower, dualnicbc, dualnicbcha, tbc, all, tgm

**TL;DR:** Three independent `main`-branch regressions — a test key-scheme bug, a broken PMC invocation, and a T-BC topology mismatch — plus a ts2phc servo regression in the upstream sync caused all 36 failures.

---

## Root Cause Groups

- **2/36 failures — `createStoredEvent()` key-scheme change drops LOCKED state** (suites: bc, dualfollower)
  Commit `d20ffcbf` (PR #171, "CNF-19588") changed `test/pkg/event/event.go`'s `createStoredEvent()` to key the `StoredEventValues` map by `v.Resource` (ResourceAddress) instead of `v.DataType`. For `OsClockSyncState` events both the notification ("LOCKED") and metric ("-18") share the identical ResourceAddress, so the metric silently overwrites the notification in the loop. The test then reads `values["notification"]` and finds nothing, `wasLocked` is never set, and the test times out — even though the production cloud-event-proxy correctly delivered LOCKED.

- **21/36 failures — PMC command split + BC/HA clock stuck at FREERUN (clock class 248)** (suites: dualnicbc, dualnicbcha)
  Commit `14eb788` (PR #629, "Sync from upstream 22-Jul-2026" in `k8snetworkplumbingwg/linuxptp-daemon`) introduced a behavioral regression where pmc receives `GET` and `PARENT_DATA_SET` as two separate argv tokens instead of a single quoted string, returning `bad command: GET` / `bad command: PARENT_DATA_SET` for every PMC call. This prevents the test from reading `parentPortIdentity` or `grandmasterIdentity`, causing role-assertion failures (`ens2f0np0` stays in MASTER instead of SLAVE) and preventing clock class from ever reaching 6. All downstream clock-sync, outage-recovery, event-API, and metrics tests cascade from this single invocation bug.

- **2/36 failures — T-BC topology solver returns zero solutions** (suites: tbc, all)
  Commit `84723c83` (PR #205, "test: Add T-BC CI tests and configuration") added `PtpConfigTelcoBC()` and its `AlgoTelcoBCString="TBC"` constraint set to `test/pkg/testconfig/testconfig.go`, requiring a WPC NIC with receiver + two same-NIC transmitter ports and a co-located WPC GM. The CI cluster (`cnfdf30`–`cnfdf32`) does not have this physical topology — only `cnfdf32` has WPC hardware (confirmed as the TGM node). `SynchronizedBeforeSuite` calls `CreatePtpConfigurationsWithRetry(3)`, the solver returns empty, and the suite is torn down before any test runs.

- **11/36 failures — WPC T-GM ts2phc servo stuck in FREERUN despite DPLL LOCKED** (suite: tgm)
  Also attributable to commit `14eb788` (PR #629 upstream sync). DPLL hardware on `cnfdf32` reports LOCKED (`dpll=1`) confirming valid GNSS/1PPS, but ts2phc software servo stays at FREERUN (`ts2phc=0`), indicating a regression in ts2phc log parsing, servo state-machine advancement, or GM clock-class propagation introduced by the sync (`log_parsing.go:82–153`, `ProcessTs2PhcEvents` in `daemon.go:2134–2190`). With ts2phc in FREERUN, `HandleDelayedPhc2sysStartup` never fires, phc2sys stays down (process_status=0), ptp4l clock class stays at 248, no CloudEvent LOCKED events are emitted, and all log-stream tests hit context deadline.

1. **Revert or fix `14eb788` (PR #629 upstream sync) in `k8snetworkplumbingwg/linuxptp-daemon`** — This single commit accounts for 32/36 failures across dualnicbc, dualnicbcha, and tgm. 2. **Fix `createStoredEvent()` key collision in `test/pkg/event/event.go`** (commit `d20ffcbf`, PR #171) — Change the `StoredEventValues` map key from `v.Resource` alone to a composite `<ResourceAddress>:<DataType>` (or revert to `v.DataType`). Add a unit test asserting that a `CLOCK_REALTIME` event with both a notification and a metric entry produces two distinct map entries.

3. **Add a `Skip()` guard in the T-BC suite setup** (commit `84723c83`, PR #205) — In `PtpConfigTelcoBC()` or the T-BC `SynchronizedBeforeSuite`, replace the hard `Expect(err).To(BeNil())` with a `Skip()` when the topology solver returns no solution. This prevents 2 suite-level failures and unblocks CI reporting for the rest of the job. Separately, work with the lab team to provision a WPC node satisfying the T-BC constraint (receiver + ≥2 same-NIC transmitters + co-located WPC GM) so the test can eventually run end-to-end.

### Suite: bc (1 failures)

**Suite TL;DR:** The single bc-parallel failure is caused by a test-code regression in `createStoredEvent()` that changed the StoredEventValues map key from `v.DataType` ("notification"/"metric") to `v.Resource` (full ResourceAddress), silently dropping the LOCKED state so the test can never observe it.

**Root Cause Groups:**

- **Group 1: Test code key-scheme change in `createStoredEvent()` silently hides LOCKED state** (affects: `[It] [bc-parallel] Event based tests PTP Slave Clock Sync`)
  - **Evidence:**
    ```
    [ptp.go: 411] got map[eventsource:/sync/sync-status/os-clock-sync-state
      eventtimestamp:2026-07-29 09:44:07.684026654 +0000 UTC
      eventtype:event.sync.sync-status.os-clock-sync-state-change
      eventvalues:map[/cluster/node/cnfdf30.telco5gran.eng.rdu2.redhat.com/CLOCK_REALTIME:-18]]
    [ptp.go: 419] clockOffset=0.000000
    [FAILED] OS Clock was never LOCKED and test timed out
    In [It] at: /tmp/cnf-pDNPW/ptp-operator-conformance-test/test/conformance/parallel/ptp.go:393
    ```
    The raw cloud event data (logged by `event.go: 730`) clearly shows:
    ```json
    {"values":[
      {"ResourceAddress":"...CLOCK_REALTIME","data_type":"notification","value_type":"enumeration","value":"LOCKED"},
      {"ResourceAddress":"...CLOCK_REALTIME","data_type":"metric","value_type":"decimal64.3","value":"-18"}
    ]}
    ```
    The LOCKED event was delivered, but `values["notification"]` and `values["metric"]` were both `nil` in the test.

  - **Root Cause:** Commit `d20ffcbf` (PR #171, `CNF-19588`) changed `createStoredEvent()` in `test/pkg/event/event.go` (v1 path lines 711–717, v2 path lines 742–751) from using `v.DataType` as the map key to using `v.Resource` (the ResourceAddress). For `OsClockSyncState` events the notification value and metric value **share the same ResourceAddress** (`/cluster/node/.../CLOCK_REALTIME`), so the metric entry (`-18`) overwrites the notification entry (`LOCKED`) in the loop. The test at `ptp.go:414-415` then reads `values["notification"]` and `values["metric"]` — both return nil because those keys no longer exist — so `state` is `""` instead of `"LOCKED"`, `wasLocked` is never set `true`, and the test times out at `ptp.go:393`.

This is a `main`-only test code change; the `release-5.0` production images are unaffected. The OS clock on the hardware IS reaching LOCKED — the cloud event confirms it — but the test framework can't see it.

  - **Is it a flake?** No — the bug is deterministic. Every run will fail to observe LOCKED until the test times out.

  - **Suggested Fix:** In `test/pkg/event/event.go`'s `createStoredEvent()`, use a composite key `<ResourceAddress>:<DataType>` (or fall back to `DataType` when ResourceAddress is empty), so that OsClockSyncState events retain distinct "notification" and "metric" entries while BC clock class events with multiple "metric" values on different resources still don't collide. Alternatively, update `ptp.go:414-415` to iterate the values map and match by DataType rather than by fixed string keys.

**Suite Severity:** HIGH

## bc

### Suite: bc (1 failures)

**Suite TL;DR:** The single bc-parallel failure is caused by a test-code regression in `createStoredEvent()` that changed the StoredEventValues map key from `v.DataType` ("notification"/"metric") to `v.Resource` (full ResourceAddress), silently dropping the LOCKED state so the test can never observe it.

**Root Cause Groups:**

- **Group 1: Test code key-scheme change in `createStoredEvent()` silently hides LOCKED state** (affects: `[It] [bc-parallel] Event based tests PTP Slave Clock Sync`)
  - **Evidence:**
    ```
    [ptp.go: 411] got map[eventsource:/sync/sync-status/os-clock-sync-state
      eventtimestamp:2026-07-29 09:44:07.684026654 +0000 UTC
      eventtype:event.sync.sync-status.os-clock-sync-state-change
      eventvalues:map[/cluster/node/cnfdf30.telco5gran.eng.rdu2.redhat.com/CLOCK_REALTIME:-18]]
    [ptp.go: 419] clockOffset=0.000000
    [FAILED] OS Clock was never LOCKED and test timed out
    In [It] at: /tmp/cnf-pDNPW/ptp-operator-conformance-test/test/conformance/parallel/ptp.go:393
    ```
    The raw cloud event data (logged by `event.go: 730`) clearly shows:
    ```json
    {"values":[
      {"ResourceAddress":"...CLOCK_REALTIME","data_type":"notification","value_type":"enumeration","value":"LOCKED"},
      {"ResourceAddress":"...CLOCK_REALTIME","data_type":"metric","value_type":"decimal64.3","value":"-18"}
    ]}
    ```
    The LOCKED event was delivered, but `values["notification"]` and `values["metric"]` were both `nil` in the test.

  - **Root Cause:** Commit `d20ffcbf` (PR #171, `CNF-19588`) changed `createStoredEvent()` in `test/pkg/event/event.go` (v1 path lines 711–717, v2 path lines 742–751) from using `v.DataType` as the map key to using `v.Resource` (the ResourceAddress). For `OsClockSyncState` events the notification value and metric value **share the same ResourceAddress** (`/cluster/node/.../CLOCK_REALTIME`), so the metric entry (`-18`) overwrites the notification entry (`LOCKED`) in the loop. The test at `ptp.go:414-415` then reads `values["notification"]` and `values["metric"]` — both return nil because those keys no longer exist — so `state` is `""` instead of `"LOCKED"`, `wasLocked` is never set `true`, and the test times out at `ptp.go:393`.

  - **Breaking PR/Commit:** Commit `d20ffcbf0cecd1cf94987788c703fa8d4565ba4d` — "CNF-19588: CI test for clockClass recovery after cloud-event-proxy crash" (merged as [PR #171](https://github.com/k8snetworkplumbingwg/ptp-operator/pull/171) on `main`). This is a `main`-only test code change; the `release-5.0` production images are unaffected. The OS clock on the hardware IS reaching LOCKED — the cloud event confirms it — but the test framework can't see it.

  - **Is it a flake?** No — the bug is deterministic. Every run will fail to observe LOCKED until the test times out.

  - **Suggested Fix:** In `test/pkg/event/event.go`'s `createStoredEvent()`, use a composite key `<ResourceAddress>:<DataType>` (or fall back to `DataType` when ResourceAddress is empty), so that OsClockSyncState events retain distinct "notification" and "metric" entries while BC clock class events with multiple "metric" values on different resources still don't collide. Alternatively, update `ptp.go:414-415` to iterate the values map and match by DataType rather than by fixed string keys.

**Suite Issue Class:** test_regression
**Suite Severity:** HIGH

### Suite: dualfollower (1 failures)

**Suite TL;DR:** The single dualfollower failure is a deterministic test regression introduced in `main`'s test parsing code — events ARE delivered by the production image but the test script can no longer extract the LOCKED state from them, causing an inevitable timeout.

**Root Cause Groups:**

- **Group 1: `createStoredEvent` key-scheme change silently drops LOCKED state, making `wasLocked` permanently false** (affects: `[It] [dualfollower-parallel] Event based tests PTP Slave Clock Sync`)
  - **Evidence:**
    ```
    DEBUG [Jul 29 09:44:44.699][event.go: 730] Context Attributes,
        type: event.sync.sync-status.os-clock-sync-state-change
      Data,
        {"version":"1.0","values":[
          {"ResourceAddress":"/cluster/node/cnfdf30.../CLOCK_REALTIME","data_type":"notification","value_type":"enumeration","value":"LOCKED"},
          {"ResourceAddress":"/cluster/node/cnfdf30.../CLOCK_REALTIME","data_type":"metric","value_type":"decimal64.3","value":"-18"}
        ]}

    DEBUG [Jul 29 09:44:44.700][ptp.go: 411] got map[eventsource:/sync/sync-status/os-clock-sync-state
      eventvalues:map[/cluster/node/cnfdf30.telco5gran.eng.rdu2.redhat.com/CLOCK_REALTIME:-18]]

    DEBUG [Jul 29 09:44:44.700][ptp.go: 419] clockOffset=0.000000

    [FAILED] OS Clock was never LOCKED and test timed out
    In [It] at: /tmp/cnf-pDNPW/ptp-operator-conformance-test/test/conformance/parallel/ptp.go:393
    ```
  - **Root Cause:** Commit `d20ffcbf` ("CNF-19588: CI test for clockClass recovery after cloud-event-proxy crash", 2026-07-03) changed `createStoredEvent()` in `test/pkg/event/event.go` to use `v.Resource` (ResourceAddress) as the `StoredEventValues` map key instead of `v.DataType`. For `OsClockSyncStateChange` events, both the notification entry ("LOCKED") and the metric entry ("-18") carry the **identical** ResourceAddress (`/cluster/node/.../CLOCK_REALTIME`), so the metric value silently overwrites the notification value, leaving a one-entry map keyed by the path. The test at `ptp.go:414` then does `values["notification"].(string)`, which finds nothing (key is now a full resource path, not "notification"), so `state` is always `""`, `wasLocked` is never set to `true`, and the test times out at `ptp.go:393`. The cloud-event-proxy production image (`release-5.0`) is delivering the LOCKED event correctly — the bug is entirely in the test-framework parsing code on `main`. Because the job pulls test scripts from `main` (`TEST_BRANCH=main`), this commit is the direct root cause.
  - **Breaking PR/Commit:** `d20ffcbf` — "CNF-19588: CI test for clockClass recovery after cloud-event-proxy crash" (2026-07-03, author jackding@gmail.com) — see https://github.com/openshift/ptp-operator/commit/d20ffcbf0cecd1cf94987788c703fa8d4565ba4d
  - **Is it a flake?** No — this is deterministic; every run with this test code and this event shape will produce the same timeout.
  - **Suggested Fix:** In `createStoredEvent()` (`test/pkg/event/event.go` lines ~711–718 for v1, ~742–752 for v2), when the ResourceAddress is non-empty, store values under **both** the resource path key AND the `DataType` key (or always use `DataType` as the primary key and resource path as a secondary key for BC multi-metric disambiguation). Alternatively, update the consumer in `ptp.go:413–415` to iterate over `values` looking for a string value equal to `"LOCKED"` or `"FREERUN"` rather than hardcoding `values["notification"]`.

**Suite Issue Class:** test_regression
**Suite Severity:** MEDIUM

## Cross-Suite Summary — periodic-ci-openshift-release-main-nightly-5.0-e2e-telco5g-ptp-upstream

**Version:** 5.0 | **Total failures:** 36 | **Suites:** bc, dualfollower, dualnicbc, dualnicbcha, tbc, all, tgm

**TL;DR:** Three independent `main`-branch regressions — a test key-scheme bug, a broken PMC invocation, and a T-BC topology mismatch — plus a ts2phc servo regression in the upstream sync caused all 36 failures.

---

## Root Cause Groups

- **2/36 failures — `createStoredEvent()` key-scheme change drops LOCKED state** (suites: bc, dualfollower)
  Commit `d20ffcbf` (PR #171, "CNF-19588") changed `test/pkg/event/event.go`'s `createStoredEvent()` to key the `StoredEventValues` map by `v.Resource` (ResourceAddress) instead of `v.DataType`. For `OsClockSyncState` events both the notification ("LOCKED") and metric ("-18") share the identical ResourceAddress, so the metric silently overwrites the notification in the loop. The test then reads `values["notification"]` and finds nothing, `wasLocked` is never set, and the test times out — even though the production cloud-event-proxy correctly delivered LOCKED.

- **21/36 failures — PMC command split + BC/HA clock stuck at FREERUN (clock class 248)** (suites: dualnicbc, dualnicbcha)
  Commit `14eb788` (PR #629, "Sync from upstream 22-Jul-2026" in `k8snetworkplumbingwg/linuxptp-daemon`) introduced a behavioral regression where pmc receives `GET` and `PARENT_DATA_SET` as two separate argv tokens instead of a single quoted string, returning `bad command: GET` / `bad command: PARENT_DATA_SET` for every PMC call. This prevents the test from reading `parentPortIdentity` or `grandmasterIdentity`, causing role-assertion failures (`ens2f0np0` stays in MASTER instead of SLAVE) and preventing clock class from ever reaching 6. All downstream clock-sync, outage-recovery, event-API, and metrics tests cascade from this single invocation bug.

- **2/36 failures — T-BC topology solver returns zero solutions** (suites: tbc, all)
  Commit `84723c83` (PR #205, "test: Add T-BC CI tests and configuration") added `PtpConfigTelcoBC()` and its `AlgoTelcoBCString="TBC"` constraint set to `test/pkg/testconfig/testconfig.go`, requiring a WPC NIC with receiver + two same-NIC transmitter ports and a co-located WPC GM. The CI cluster (`cnfdf30`–`cnfdf32`) does not have this physical topology — only `cnfdf32` has WPC hardware (confirmed as the TGM node). `SynchronizedBeforeSuite` calls `CreatePtpConfigurationsWithRetry(3)`, the solver returns empty, and the suite is torn down before any test runs.

- **11/36 failures — WPC T-GM ts2phc servo stuck in FREERUN despite DPLL LOCKED** (suite: tgm)
  Also attributable to commit `14eb788` (PR #629 upstream sync). DPLL hardware on `cnfdf32` reports LOCKED (`dpll=1`) confirming valid GNSS/1PPS, but ts2phc software servo stays at FREERUN (`ts2phc=0`), indicating a regression in ts2phc log parsing, servo state-machine advancement, or GM clock-class propagation introduced by the sync (`log_parsing.go:82–153`, `ProcessTs2PhcEvents` in `daemon.go:2134–2190`). With ts2phc in FREERUN, `HandleDelayedPhc2sysStartup` never fires, phc2sys stays down (process_status=0), ptp4l clock class stays at 248, no CloudEvent LOCKED events are emitted, and all log-stream tests hit context deadline.
